Fact.Name: PFIC mark-to-market positions
Fact.Description: Marketable PFIC stock positions held at year end. Record a separate position for each owner and basis lot. An explicitly empty collection means there are no positions; an unanswered collection has no computed total.

Fact.Name: Owner of the PFIC position
Fact.Description: The United States individual who owns this position, including a proportionately owned interest through a foreign entity. Values and basis entered for this position must be this owner's share, not the issuer's or entity's entire holding.

Fact.Name: Section 1296 election applies to this marketable position
Fact.Description: Is a valid mark-to-market election in effect for this owner's marketable PFIC stock held at year end? The election continues in subsequent years unless the stock ceases to be marketable or revocation is permitted. Answer false for a position outside this regime; this does not exclude it from other PFIC rules.

Fact.Name: First-year excess-distribution coordination required
Fact.Description: Does the first-year coordination rule in section 1296(j) apply? Answer true when the election starts after the holding period began and the continuous qualified-electing-fund exception is not met. Such a position requires the first-year excess-distribution computation and cannot be treated as an ordinary annual mark.

Fact.Name: Year-end fair market value
Fact.Description: Fair market value in dollars of this owner's stock at the close of the tax year.

Fact.Name: Adjusted basis before the annual mark
Fact.Description: Adjusted basis of this owner's stock immediately before this year's mark. Include applicable inherited-stock and new-US-person basis rules in section 1296(i) and (l); do not enter original purchase cost in place of adjusted basis.

Fact.Name: Prior mark-to-market inclusions
Fact.Description: Total prior-year inclusions for this stock under section 1296(d), including amounts that would have been included but for the first-year excess-distribution coordination. Enter zero explicitly if there are none.

Fact.Name: Prior mark-to-market deductions
Fact.Description: Total deductions allowed for this stock in prior years under the mark-to-market rules. Enter zero explicitly if there are none.

Fact.Name: Signed annual mark already included elsewhere in NIIT
Fact.Description: The signed part of this same annual mark already reflected on another Form 8960 line: positive for included gain, negative for a deducted loss. Enter zero explicitly if none. Do not include any unrelated income, distribution or sale.

Fact.Name: Prior unreversed mark-to-market inclusions
Fact.Description: Excess, if any, of prior mark-to-market inclusions over prior deductions for this stock.

Fact.Name: Signed annual mark-to-market income or deduction
Fact.Description: Appreciation is included in income; a decline is deductible only to the extent of unreversed prior inclusions. A position outside this election contributes zero to this regime. First-year coordination and unanswered inputs leave this computation Incomplete.

Fact.Name: Adjusted basis after the annual mark
Fact.Description: Basis before the annual mark increased by the inclusion or decreased by the allowed deduction.

Fact.Name: Unreversed inclusions after the annual mark
Fact.Description: Prior unreversed inclusions increased by this year's inclusion or reduced by this year's allowed deduction.

Fact.Name: PFIC annual mark not already reflected in NIIT
Fact.Description: Signed annual mark less the portion already included elsewhere on Form 8960. This prevents counting the same gain or deduction twice.

Fact.Name: Total annual PFIC ordinary mark-to-market income
Fact.Description: Total annual ordinary inclusions less allowed annual deductions for the entered PFIC positions. First-year coordination is not an ordinary inclusion and leaves this total Incomplete.

Fact.Name: Total PFIC annual mark adjustment for Form 8960 line 6
Fact.Description: Total signed PFIC annual-mark adjustment not otherwise reflected on Form 8960. An answered empty collection contributes zero; an unanswered collection or unresolved position leaves the total Incomplete.

Fact.Name: This return's MFJ status rests on the section 6013(g)/(h) NRA spouse election
Fact.Description: True when form1040:/writableForm1040NonresidentAlienSpouseElection is answered true — the return-level record of the section 6013(g) or 6013(h) election a U.S. citizen or resident makes to file jointly with a nonresident alien spouse. Complete-safe (IsComplete-guarded), so a return that never answers the election resolves false and /niitThreshold falls through to its ordinary filing-status switch, unchanged. Named separately from /niitAppliesSection6013ElectionForNiitPurposes because the two are DIFFERENT elections: this one is made on the return itself and sets MFJ filing status; the other is made on Form 8960 and decides only whether the MFJ threshold follows that status for NIIT purposes.

Fact.Name: The section 6013(g)/(h) election is also applied for NIIT purposes (Form 8960 Part I checkbox)
Fact.Description: True when the filer checked the Form 8960 Part I section 6013(g) or section 6013(h) election box — /writableNiitSection6013gElection or /writableNiitSection6013hElection — which the instructions describe as a SEPARATE election from the section 6013(g)/(h) election that sets the return's own filing status: "you can also elect to apply the joint return election for NIIT purposes," made "for NIIT purposes" by checking "the appropriate checkbox near the top of Form 8960, Part I." A filer who made the underlying election (form1040:/writableForm1040NonresidentAlienSpouseElection, which sets the return's MFJ filing status) but leaves both Form 8960 boxes unanswered has NOT applied it for NIIT purposes, and /niitThreshold reads this fact to decide whether the MFJ or the MFS threshold governs. Unanswered on either box resolves false, matching the printed default: "If you made a section 6013(g) or 6013(h) election to file jointly with your NRA spouse, but don't also elect to apply the joint return election for NIIT purposes, then, for NIIT purposes, you'll file as married filing separately." Complete-safe (IsComplete-guarded per box, then Any), so an ordinary MFJ return with no NRA spouse keeps /niitThreshold Complete and, because /niitFilingJointlyUnderNraSpouseElection is false on every such return, this fact never changes its threshold.

Fact.Name: NIIT MAGI threshold based on filing status (Form 8960 line 14)
Fact.Description: The §1411 threshold (Form 8960 line 14): $250,000 MFJ or QSS, $125,000 MFS, $200,000 single or HoH. Reuses the existing /netInvestmentIncomeThreshold* constants (which correctly group QSS with MFJ — unlike the Additional Medicare Tax threshold, where QSS groups with single).

Fact.Name: Net gain or (loss) from disposition of property for NIIT (Form 8960 line 5a), complete-safe
Fact.Description:
Form 8960 line 5a "Net gain or loss from disposition of property", which the Lines 5a-5d Net Gains and Losses Worksheet calls line 1, "Beginning net gains and losses" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8960.pdf, page 10, its "Enter this amount on line 5a" pointer at lines 649-652). THIS FACT HELD THE PATH /netCapitalGainForNiit before the 5b/5c split, and its body is unchanged by the move: it was the whole of lines 5a THROUGH 5d while 5b and 5c were deferred, and when those two entry lines landed as attested writables the combine moved to /netCapitalGainForNiit (line 5d) and this expression kept the line it always computed. No dollar moved in the split, which is every committed scenario. The Line 5a instruction paragraph combines TWO amounts from the return: Form 1040 line 7a AND Schedule 1 (Form 1040) line 4. Term one (line 7a) = income:/capitalGainsOrLosses — which already combines BOTH capital-gain paths (the Schedule D net after the $3,000/$1,500 loss floor, and the "Schedule D not required" 1099-DIV box-2a direct term), so it captures the Schedule-D gain AND the box-2a-only gain with no double count. Term two (Schedule 1 line 4) = form4797:/form4797OrdinaryIncome — the Form 4797 ordinary gain/loss (§1245 depreciation recapture + net §1231 recharacterization + Part II ordinary +, , the Form 4797 line 14 Form 4684 Section B casualty leg) that was PREVIOUSLY OMITTED, under-computing NIIT on a return with a §1245 recapture on passive property (see the authority comment). THAT PARENTHETICAL LISTED THREE ADDENDS UNTIL THE LINE-14 LEG LANDED; it is four now, and the fourth is SIGNED NEGATIVE across the whole Section B population this build models, so it enters term two as a subtraction. Both terms are wrapped complete-safe (IsComplete → else 0): although income:/capitalGainsOrLosses already resolves Complete on every full-computation return (it feeds /totalIncome), the guard keeps /netInvestmentIncome Complete on any partial-computation scenario (e.g. an EITC-eligibility golden that never resolves line 7), so this fact never drops /line21OfSchedule2 from its prior completeness — this resolves the "5d Placeholder blocker" the module comment named. LINE 5a MAY BE NEGATIVE: the Form 1040 line-7a capital term is NOT floored. A current-year net capital loss (already limited to -$3,000/-$1,500 by the Schedule D line-21 loss limitation, and reflecting any prior-year carry-IN) flows through and REDUCES net investment income, exactly as the Form 8960 line-5a worksheet takes Form 1040 line 7a directly (the worksheet's capital-loss carry-OUT add-back, line 2(i), feeds line 5b — where it sits inside the attested residual /writableNiitLine5bOtherExcludedAmounts, not itemized — never line 5a). The prior GreaterOf(term1 + term2, 0) floor clamped a net loss to 0, OVER-stating NII on a net-loss return and over-charging the taxpayer ~$114 on a $3,000 loss — "conservative" for the FISC, not for the filer (the government-side mislabel.)
THE SCHEDULE 1 LINE-4 (FORM 4797 ORDINARY) TERM IS NOW SIGNED TOO. The per-term floor that used to stand on it — GreaterOf(form4797:/form4797OrdinaryIncome, 0), which added only a POSITIVE Form 4797 gain and held out an ordinary LOSS of undeterminable §1411 character — is GONE, and its removal is the value-moving half of this landing. The printed form never worked that way. Worksheet line 1, "Beginning net gains and losses", takes column (A) Form 1040 line 7a and column (B) Schedule 1 (Form 1040) line 4 WHOLE AND SIGNED (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8960.pdf, page 10), and the exclusion the floor stood in for has its own printed home one row down: worksheet rows 2(a) and 2(b) ask the filer, per trade or business, for the gains and the losses on property used in a NON-section 1411 trade or business, and route the answer to line 5b (lines 654-667). The printed default is include-everything-on-line-5a, then let the filer exclude on line 5b.
NEITHER HALF IS SAFE ALONE, which is why they land in one unit. Removing the floor by itself ships the printed default with no exclusion mechanism, so a non-§1411 ACTIVE-business Form 4797 loss would reduce NII on every return — the unguarded under-computation an earlier triage refused, and it was right to. Building rows 2(a)/2(b) by themselves changes nothing, because line 5b may only move amounts "included on line 5a" (lines 602-606) and the floor's victim never reached line 5a. Together they are the printed mechanism.
THE DIRECTION THIS MOVES, disclosed where the old floor's "DISCLOSED BENEFICIARY: the fisc" note used to sit, because a direction change stated nowhere is what an audit would catch. BEFORE: a Form 4797 ordinary loss could never reduce NII, so the model could only OVER-state NIIT on that term. AFTER: it reduces NII unless the filer attests on row 2(b) that the property was used in a non-§1411 trade or business. An UNATTESTED non-§1411 loss therefore now lowers NIIT where it previously did not. That is the printed allocation of the burden — /form4797OrdinaryIncome carries no §1411, passive or material-participation attribute of any kind, so the filer's row-2(b) answer is the only §1411 test that exists — and the model asks the printed question rather than guessing an answer in either direction.
A SCOPING PARAGRAPH THAT DIED WITH THE FLOOR, recorded so a reader does not go looking for it: while the floor stood, it wrapped /form4797OrdinaryIncome, which is ALREADY the sum of that form's four ordinary addends, so the addends netted BEFORE the floor saw them and a loss addend riding alongside a larger positive one reduced NII with no §1411 test at all. The floor was on the FORM, not on the LOSS. With the floor gone the asymmetry is gone with it: every addend, positive or negative, reaches line 5a on the same terms, and row 2(b) is the one place §1411 character is asked. The MIXED-CASE note that sat here — a capital gain paired with a Form 4797 ordinary loss no longer netting — is likewise dissolved; the two now net, as worksheet line 1 prints them.
Net investment income (line 12, /netInvestmentIncome) stays floored at 0, so this signed term can never drive NII below 0. The Schedule 1 line 4 term and the line-7a floor removal are both reflected here; split out of /netCapitalGainForNiit onto its own printed entry line when 5b/5c landed; the line-4 floor was removed together with the worksheet rows 2(a)/2(b) column (B) intakes below.

Fact.Name: Lines 5a-5d Worksheet row 2(a), column (B) — net ordinary GAINS from property used in a non-section 1411 trade or business (writable)
Fact.Description:
Worksheet row 2(a) of the Lines 5a-5d Net Gains and Losses Worksheet, COLUMN (B) ONLY: "Enter net gains from the disposition of property used in a non-section 1411 trade or business (enter as negative amounts): Name of trade or business / Amount" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8960.pdf, page 10), where column (B) is "Ordinary gains/(losses): Schedule 1 (Form 1040), line 4" (lines 635-648). Column (B) IS the Schedule 1 line-4 term of /niitLine5aNetGainFromDisposition, which is why this row and its 2(b) twin are the printed exclusion mechanism for that term.
SIGN: NEGATIVE, and a Max-at-zero Limit DECLARES that bound. The printed parenthesis says "enter as negative amounts" and the row's column cells are printed with the accountant's parentheses (line 657). An excluded gain entered negative reduces line 5b, which reduces line 5d, which reduces NII — the filer is taking a gain the model included on line 5a back out of NII because the property was used in a trade or business that is NOT a section 1411 activity.
WHAT THE LIMIT DOES AND DOES NOT DO, measured at this landing rather than assumed, because the sentence that used to sit here said the Limit "enforces" the sign and that is only half true. The declaration fires as a validation Error — scripts/limit_test.py drives every declared Limit out of bounds through runner --validate and this one is in its 445, none skipped — so the intake surface and the validation pass both refuse a positive entry. RESOLUTION DOES NOT. A scratch probe answered this field +6,860 on the Pub 544 return and the graph resolved it at face value: line 5b came out +6,860 and line 5d 15,020 instead of 1,300, i.e. a mis-signed entry RAISES NII by the amount the filer meant to remove, doubling the error rather than losing it. So the bound is real but it lives at validation, and the consequence is named here because a Description that leans on an unverified guard is the wrong-looking-right class this repo keeps paying for.
RETURN-LEVEL TOTAL, NOT A PER-BUSINESS COLLECTION, and that is a deliberate reading of the printed table rather than a simplification of it. The row prints a "Name of trade or business / Amount" list whose cells sum into one column-(B) figure, and the figure is what line 2(j) consumes; the names are captioning, not arithmetic. Under the engine-capability bar's clause (b) the printed structure's own bound is a short list summing to a total, so the total is the faithful model and the collection would add a data model the arithmetic never reads. The names belong to a statement surface, not to this graph (invariant #7).
WHY THIS EXISTS AT ALL: it is the guard half of the floor removal. Before it, the Schedule 1 line-4 term of line 5a was floored at zero, which excluded EVERY Form 4797 ordinary loss whether or not it was section 1411 in character. Removing that floor without this row would ship the printed default with no way to exclude anything; shipping this row without removing the floor would be dead code, since line 5b may only move amounts "included on line 5a" (lines 602-606) and a floored-out loss is not included on line 5a. Neither half is safe alone, which is the claim /netCapitalGainForNiit's retired contract made and which this landing re-derived from the printed worksheet before acting on it.
ADDITIVE: no committed scenario answers this field, so it is Incomplete corpus-wide and contributes no resolved row; its complete-safe reading lives inline in /niitLine5bExcludedDisposition.

Fact.Name: Lines 5a-5d Worksheet row 2(b), column (B) — net ordinary LOSSES from property used in a non-section 1411 trade or business (writable)
Fact.Description:
Worksheet row 2(b) of the Lines 5a-5d Net Gains and Losses Worksheet, COLUMN (B) ONLY: "Enter net losses from the disposition of property used in a non-section 1411 trade or business (enter as positive amounts): Name of trade or business / Amount" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8960.pdf, page 10), column (B) being "Ordinary gains/(losses): Schedule 1 (Form 1040), line 4" (lines 635-648).
THIS ROW IS THE GUARD THE FLOOR REMOVAL NEEDED, and it is the more important of the pair. Its sign is POSITIVE — an excluded LOSS entered positive RAISES line 5b, raises line 5d and raises NII, undoing the reduction the loss made on line 5a. So a filer whose Form 4797 ordinary loss came from a trade or business they materially participate in (a non-section 1411 activity, IRC 1411(c)(2)(A)) enters it here and the loss stops reducing NII. That is the printed replacement for the per-term floor this module used to carry: the floor guessed "every 4797 loss is non-1411"; this row asks. A Min-at-zero Limit DECLARES the printed sign, on the same terms as its 2(a) twin one fact up — it fires at validation (limit_test drives it out of bounds) but resolution takes any answer at face value. The probe measured that too, and this is the direction that matters: answered at -840 instead of +840, line 5b came out -840 and line 5d -1,680, so a mis-signed entry DOUBLES the loss's NII-reducing effect instead of cancelling it. That is the under-computing direction, which is why the sign is stated three times over — in the printed row text, in the declaration, and here.
THE OTHER ORDER IS WRONG TOO, AND IT WAS MEASURED, NOT ARGUED. That is the concrete reason this row could not ship first and wait for the floor: shipping it alone is not merely inert, it is wrong on any return that answers it. The same probe measured the other arm at 1,900 against 1,868, which is the floor's own effect. Both halves, one landing.
RETURN-LEVEL TOTAL, for the same printed-structure reason as its 2(a) twin one fact up.
ADDITIVE: no committed scenario answers this field.

Fact.Name: Lines 5a-5d Worksheet row 2(e) — the net gain attributable to net unrealized appreciation in employer securities (writable)
Fact.Description:
SCREEN. Question: "How much of your gain on a disposition of employer securities was attributable to net unrealized appreciation while the securities were held by the qualified plan?" Help text: worksheet row 2(e) of the Lines 5a-5d Net Gains and Losses Worksheet is "Enter the net gain attributable to the net unrealized appreciation (NUA) in employer securities", and the instructions state the rule behind it: "Any gain attributable to NUA (within the meaning of section 402(e)(4)) that you realize on a disposition of employer securities held by a qualified plan is a distribution within the meaning of section 1411(c)(5) and isn't included in NII." So this is a distribution excluded from net investment income, entered here to take it back out of line 5a.
WHERE THE EXCLUSION STOPS, and the sentence that follows is as important as the one before it: "any gain realized on a disposition of employer securities attributable to appreciation in the value of your employer securities AFTER the distribution from a qualified plan isn't a distribution within the meaning of section 1411(c)(5) and IS included in NII." Only the appreciation that accrued INSIDE the plan comes out; everything the securities gained after they were distributed stays in.
THIS IS THE LATER DISPOSITION, NOT THE DISTRIBUTION EVENT. The amount belongs to the year the filer SELLS the employer securities, and the gain that reaches Form 8960 line 5a through Form 1040 line 7a is what this row removes. It is not the Form 1099-R box 6 figure reported in the year of the lump-sum distribution.
SIGN: NEGATIVE, and a Max-at-zero Limit declares that bound. The row's printed amount cell carries the accountant's parentheses and line 5b's own sign rule is "Enter the amount of gains (as a negative number) and losses (as a positive number) included on line 5a that are excluded from NII" — an excluded GAIN is negative and reduces net investment income. The same measurement row 2(a) records applies here: the Limit fires as a validation Error and NOT at resolution, so a positive entry would RAISE net investment income by the amount the filer meant to remove.
COLUMN (A) BY NATURE. A gain on a disposition of employer securities is a capital gain, so this row belongs to worksheet column (A). Row 2(i)(1) adds this known column-(A) amount directly to the signed capital-column shares of the mixed line-5b and line-5c parents.
Asked when: the return reports a disposition of employer securities that were held by a qualified plan. Unanswered posture: DEFAULTED to $0 through /niitLine5bExcludedDisposition — an EXCLUSION intake with no condition of allowance, disclosed rather than refused, so the screen should be shown rather than skipped; a filer who never answers it keeps the whole gain in net investment income, the taxpayer-adverse direction. Validation: Dollar, Max $0, ONE return-level amount. What the answer feeds: Form 8960 line 5b -> line 5d -> line 8 -> line 12.

Fact.Name: Lines 5a-5d Worksheet row 2(h) — the prior year's worksheet row 2(i) amount, carried in (writable)
Fact.Description:
SCREEN. Question: "What amount did you enter on row 2(i) of the Form 8960 Lines 5a-5d Net Gains and Losses Worksheet on last year's return?" Help text: worksheet row 2(h) is "Enter the amount reported on line 2(i) of this worksheet from your prior tax year return calculations. Enter as a positive number." Row 2(i) is the negative capital-loss-carryforward adjustment the worksheet makes when a filer carries a capital loss forward; row 2(h) gives it back in the following year, so the exclusion is a timing adjustment rather than a permanent one. The number comes from the filer's own prior-year worksheet, which is not part of the return this system files; leave it blank if last year's row 2(i) was blank or zero.
TRANSCRIBED, NEVER CARRIED. This graph computes one tax year and holds no prior-year worksheet, so a cross-year figure is an intake the filer copies, the same treatment the Schedule D prior-year capital-loss carryovers get. Nothing here validates it against last year's return.
SIGN: POSITIVE, and a Min-at-zero Limit declares that bound, because the printed row says "Enter as a positive number" in its own words. A positive entry RAISES line 5b, which raises line 5d and net investment income — which is the point: last year's row 2(i) took an amount OUT of net investment income and this row puts it back. The row 2(a) measurement applies here too: the Limit fires as a validation Error and not at resolution.
COLUMN (A) BY NATURE, since row 2(i) is itself a capital-side adjustment; row 2(i)(1) now includes this known column-(A) amount directly.
Asked when: the return's prior-year Form 8960 worksheet carried a row 2(i) amount. Unanswered posture: DEFAULTED to $0 through /niitLine5bExcludedDisposition — disclosed. It is an INCLUSION by direction (it raises net investment income), so an unanswered box is taxpayer-FAVOURABLE, and it is nonetheless defaulted rather than refused because it is a prior-year transcription with no condition of allowance attached to this year's return; the screen should be shown rather than skipped. Validation: Dollar, Min $0, ONE return-level amount. What the answer feeds: Form 8960 line 5b -> line 5d -> line 8 -> line 12.

Fact.Name: Form 8960 line 5b — the worksheet line-2 rows this build does not itemize (writable)
Fact.Description:
THE RESIDUAL HALF of the Form 8960 line 5b entry, i.e. of the Lines 5a-5d Net Gains and Losses Worksheet line 2(j), "Sum of lines 2(a) through 2(i)", whose printed pointer is "Enter this amount on line 5b" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8960.pdf, page 10).
THIS FIELD HELD THE WHOLE OF LINE 2(j) before the row split, under the path /writableNiitLine5bExcludedDisposition, and its scope narrowed the day rows 2(a)/2(b) column (B) became intakes of their own. It was renamed rather than left in place precisely so the narrowing cannot be missed: a filer who answered the old field with a full 2(j) total AND answered the two new rows would double-exclude, and a Description warning is a weaker guard than a name that no longer promises the total. What remains here is every excluded amount this build does not itemize — rows 2(a) and 2(b) COLUMN (A), the capital side, plus rows 2(c), 2(d), 2(f), and 2(g) in both columns. Rows 2(e), 2(h), and 2(i) have separate paths. No committed scenario answered the old path, so nothing migrates.
THE SIGN CONVENTION IS THE PRINTED ONE AND IT IS THE WHOLE HAZARD OF THIS FIELD. The instruction states it once, for the entire line: "Use line 5b to adjust the amounts included on line 5a for gains and losses that are excluded from the calculation of NII. Enter the amount of gains (as a negative number) and losses (as a positive number) included on line 5a that are excluded from NII" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8960.pdf, page 9). So an excluded GAIN is entered NEGATIVE and reduces NII; an excluded LOSS is entered POSITIVE and raises NII. The worksheet prints the same rule twice more, on the two rows that carry the §1411 trade-or-business question: row 2(a) "Enter net gains from the disposition of property used in a non-section 1411 trade or business (enter as negative amounts)" and row 2(b) "Enter net losses from the disposition of property used in a non-section 1411 trade or business (enter as positive amounts)" (lines 654-663). A model that pinned only one arm would leave the sign untested in the direction that matters most, since a mis-signed excluded LOSS is the under-computing one.
SIGNED, NOT FLOORED, deliberately: this line is the only place on Form 8960 Part I where a filer can move the disposition figure in EITHER direction, and a floor in either direction would silently delete one of the two printed rows.
BOUNDED BY LINE 5a, which is the printed rule for every row of worksheet line 2 — including the two rows now modelled separately. The instruction's own words are "gains ... and losses ... INCLUDED ON LINE 5A that are excluded from NII". THIS PARAGRAPH USED TO SAY SOMETHING STRONGER AND THAT HAS BEEN FALSIFIED: it argued that the per-term Form 4797 floor on /niitLine5aNetGainFromDisposition and this entry could not double-exclude the same dollar, because an amount the floor already held out of line 5a was not "included on line 5a" and so was ineligible here. The floor is gone. The Schedule 1 line-4 term now reaches line 5a whole and signed, so a non-section 1411 Form 4797 amount IS included on line 5a and IS eligible for line 5b — which is the printed design, not a collision. What replaces the old argument is a decomposition: the section 1411 trade-or-business exclusion is asked once, on worksheet rows 2(a)/2(b) column (B), and this residual field is scoped to exclude those rows, so no dollar has two homes.
WHAT THIS STILL DOES NOT ASK, narrowed twice. Rows 2(a) and 2(b) COLUMN (B) are their own intakes, and so now are row 2(e) (the net gain attributable to net unrealized appreciation in employer securities, /writableNiitWorksheetRow2eNetUnrealizedAppreciationGain) and row 2(h) (the prior year's row 2(i), transcribed, /writableNiitWorksheetRow2hPriorYearRow2iCarryIn). WHAT STAYS INSIDE THIS ATTESTATION IS EXACTLY: rows 2(a)/2(b) COLUMN (A) — the capital side of the same trade-or-business question — and rows 2(c), 2(d), 2(f) and 2(g). Do NOT enter a row 2(e), row 2(h), or row 2(i) amount here: each has its own path and entering it twice counts it twice. When this residual is answered, also provide its signed column-(A) share at /writableNiitLine5bOtherExcludedAmountsCapitalShare if row 2(i) is live. That share is not bounded by this signed net parent: capital and ordinary components may offset, so the capital subtotal can exceed or oppose the aggregate residual. ROW 2(c) IS A FILER FIGURE IN THIS BUILD, and the reason is worth stating because a reader may expect otherwise: row 2(c) is "net losses from a former passive activity allowed by reason of section 469(f)(1)(A)", and this dictionary models no change of activity status between years at all — Form 8960 line 4b carries no former-passive leg and /niitLine4cRentalRoyaltyAndPassthroughTotal reads no 4b term — so nothing upstream can supply the figure. ROW 2(i) IS COMPUTED FROM ITS PRINTED TWO-LEG RULE below. Its leg (i)(2), "the amount of capital loss carried over to next year", reads the exported Schedule D worksheet carry-out facts. Its leg (i)(1) is the positive part of rows 2(e), 2(h), the signed column-(A) share of this residual, and the signed column-(A) share of worksheet row 3(d). Each share is required when its parent is answered and the carry-out is positive; it is not bounded by its net parent because capital and ordinary components may offset. No share is required when there is no carry-out and the printed instruction says to skip row 2(i). An incomplete live share propagates through line 5b/line 5d and Schedule 2's line-21 gate, which reads row 2(i) in the first Case guard so Incomplete cannot collapse to false.
ADDITIVE: no committed scenario answers this field, so line 5b resolves 0 corpus-wide and the only line-5d movement this landing produces comes from the line-5a floor removal. DO NOT ENTER THE UNELECTED QEF CURRENT CAPITAL INCLUSION HERE EITHER. Worksheet row 2(f) — the section 1293(a)(1)(B) long-term capital gain of a QEF for which a section 1.1411-10(g) election is not in effect — is supplied by /niitCfcQefCapitalExclusion from the per-holding CFC/QEF collection when that collection is answered, and entering it here as well excludes it twice.

Fact.Name: Form 8960 worksheet row 2(i)(1) — column (A) share of the unitemized line-5b rows (writable)
Fact.Description: SCREEN. Question: "Of the other excluded gains and losses you entered for Form 8960 line 5b, what is the signed capital gain or loss amount in worksheet column (A)?" Enter only the capital-gains/(losses) part of the residual line-5b amount (rows 2(a)/2(b) column (A), and the capital parts of rows 2(c), 2(d), 2(f), and 2(g)); use the same line-5b signs, negative for excluded gains and positive for excluded losses. Do not include rows 2(e), 2(h), or 3(d), which have their own amounts. This is an independently attested signed subtotal, not a share percentage. It is not bounded by the signed residual parent: column (A) capital and column (B) ordinary amounts can offset, so the column-(A) subtotal can exceed or oppose the net total. Asked when: the return has a positive Schedule D capital-loss carry-out for next year and /writableNiitLine5bOtherExcludedAmounts is answered. Unanswered posture: REQUIRED in that case; /niitLine5bOtherExcludedAmountsCapitalShare stays Incomplete so the row-2(i) adjustment is not guessed. It is not needed when the Schedule D carry-out is zero because the worksheet says to skip row 2(i). Validation: signed Dollar, no Min/Max. What it feeds: worksheet row 2(i)(1) → Form 8960 line 5b → line 5d → line 8 → line 12. Exclude the unelected QEF capital exclusion as well: /niitCfcQefCapitalExclusion carries its own signed column-(A) contribution into worksheet row 2(i)(1).

Fact.Name: Form 8960 line 5b — worksheet line 2(j), complete-safe
Fact.Description:
Form 8960 line 5b = Lines 5a-5d Net Gains and Losses Worksheet line 2(j), "Sum of lines 2(a) through 2(i)" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8960.pdf, page 10). WAS A BARE PASS-THROUGH of one writable; it is now the printed SUM of the worksheet's line-2 rows as this build decomposes them: row 2(a) column (B), row 2(b) column (B), the attested residual for every remaining unitemized row, and computed row 2(i). The first three terms are wrapped complete-safe (IsComplete else 0). Row 2(i) is Complete when its carry-out is zero or its required column-(A) shares are answered, and otherwise remains Incomplete so the omission is not silently treated as zero; that state must reach /netCapitalGainForNiit and /line21OfSchedule2.
WHY A SUM AND NOT A CHOICE. All four terms are components of one printed total, so they add; there is no precedence between them and no arm where one overrides another. The double-count hazard the decomposition creates is closed at the intake names, not here: the residual field is /writableNiitLine5bOtherExcludedAmounts, which does not promise the 2(j) total, and its Description scopes it to rows 2(a)/2(b) column (A) plus rows 2(c), 2(d), 2(f), and 2(g).
SIGNED, NOT FLOORED. Line 5b is the only place on Form 8960 Part I where a filer moves the disposition figure in either direction: row 2(a) is negative by print and reduces NII, row 2(b) is positive by print and raises it. The two intakes DECLARE those printed signs as Limits, which fire at validation but not at resolution (measured — see either intake's own Description); the residual and its capital subtotal are signed both ways because they aggregate rows of both kinds, and carry no Limit at all for that reason. No floor here — net investment income floors ONCE, at line 12, so a negative line 5b can never drive NIIT below zero.
CORPUS-NEUTRAL: no committed scenario answers any line-5b writable, and the base returns have no Schedule D carry-out, so every term resolves to 0.00 on those returns exactly as before the decomposition.
WORKSHEET ROW 2(f) IS THE FIFTH TERM: /niitCfcQefCapitalExclusion, the negative of the current section 1293(a)(1)(B) capital inclusion already represented in line 5a for a QEF with no section 1.1411-10(g) election in effect. It is $0 whenever the per-holding CFC/QEF collection is unanswered, so no committed return moves.

Fact.Name: Form 8960 line 5c — adjustment from disposition of partnership interest or S corporation stock (writable)
Fact.Description:
The Form 8960 line 5c entry. Its instruction is one sentence and it delegates the whole computation to the printed worksheet: "Enter the amount from the worksheet for lines 5a-5d, line 3d. Attach a statement as described under Required statements, earlier, to your return for the year of the disposition" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8960.pdf, page 12). Worksheet line 3(d) is "Combine the amounts on lines 3(a)(iii), 3(b)(iii), and 3(c)(iii)" with the pointer "Enter this amount on line 5c" (lines 764-767).
SIGNED, and the worksheet prints its own sign rule as a TIP rather than as a per-row parenthesis: "If the amount of gain for NIIT purposes is less than the amount of gain for regular income tax purposes, the entry on line 3(a)(iii), 3(b)(iii), or 3(c)(iii) should be a negative number. If the amount of loss for NIIT purposes is less than the amount of loss for regular income tax purposes, the entry ... should be a positive number" (lines 774-777). WHY THIS IS AN ATTESTATION AND NOT A COMPUTATION, and why its interior gets no contract of its own. Worksheet rows 3(a)(ii) and 3(b)(ii) both read "the amount of net gain [or loss] included in NII after the application of Regulations section 1.1411-7". That regulation is the §1411(c)(4) deemed-asset-sale computation, and TREASURY REGULATIONS ARE NOT VENDORED IN THIS REPO AT ALL — there is no sources/ path for any of them. Nothing here models a partnership or S corporation basis either. So the figure is the filer's, arrived at off this return, and modelling the interior would be false precision rather than a deferred build. That is a bounded statement about DEFINING the amount to a filer; it does not block the entry line, which the form prints as a plain dollar entry.
THE REQUIRED STATEMENT IS NOT THIS REPO'S (invariant #7). The instruction's "attach a statement" clause is an attachment surface, i.e. e-file/MeF territory, and the dictionary carries the figure only.
ADDITIVE: no committed scenario answers this field.

Fact.Name: Form 8960 line 5c, complete-safe

UNLIKE its line-5b twin this really is a bare pass-through: line 3(d)'s interior (rows 3(a) through 3(c)) is not decomposed here, because Regulations section 1.1411-7 is unvendored and nothing models a partnership or S corporation basis, so there is no row to itemize — see the writable it wraps.

Fact.Name: Column (A) share of line 5c row 3(d), required when line 5c is answered
Fact.Description: Read the signed capital-column amount only when the line-5c parent is Complete. Fact.Name: Form 8960 worksheet row 2(i)(1), signed column-(A) subtotal
Fact.Description: The signed sum of worksheet row 2(e), row 2(h), the column-(A) share of the line-5b residual, and the column-(A) share of line 5c row 3(d). Row 2(i)(1) is the positive part of this subtotal. Kept internal to the row-2(i) computation: when this subtotal is complete and non-positive, row 2(i) is $0 regardless of whether Schedule D's carry-out worksheet is complete, so the Schedule D carry-outs need not be read to prove that zero. When the subtotal is not complete, the row still checks whether Schedule D has a positive carry-out before requiring its live shares. The unelected QEF capital exclusion (/niitCfcQefCapitalExclusion, worksheet row 2(f)) is a sixth term: it is a column-(A) amount, so leaving it out of this subtotal would let a capital-loss carryforward adjustment stand on a capital column the exclusion has already reduced. $0 when the per-holding CFC/QEF collection is unanswered.

Fact.Name: Lines 5a-5d Worksheet row 2(i), capital-loss-carryforward adjustment
Fact.Description: Form 8960 Lines 5a-5d Net Gains and Losses Worksheet row 2(i). The printed instruction says to skip this row when there is no capital loss carried over to next year; otherwise enter the lesser of (i)(1) and (i)(2) as a negative amount. Here (i)(2) is the sum of Schedule D's exported short- and long-term capital loss carry-out facts. (i)(1) is the positive part of the complete-safe signed subtotal in /niitWorksheetRow2iColumnAShareBasis. An answered mixed-column parent requires its corresponding signed capital share when a positive (i)(1) may be reduced; each share is not bounded by its signed net parent because column-(A) capital and column-(B) ordinary components can offset. The zero cases are short-circuited safely: a complete non-positive (i)(1) proves row 2(i) is zero regardless of carry-out, and a zero carry-out proves the printed skip result without requiring either share. If (i)(1) is positive, the Schedule D carry-outs are read; a live missing share or unresolved carry-out stays unresolved, never silently zero. This fact is added directly to line 5b, and its path is included in the first Case guard of schedule2:/requiresSchedule2's moot-first Switch so a refusal on the NIIT chain is not collapsed to a false attachment result.

Fact.Name: Net gain or (loss) from disposition of property for NIIT (Form 8960 line 5d)
Fact.Description:
Form 8960 line 5d, "Combine lines 5a through 5c" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f8960.pdf, page 1), which the Lines 5a-5d Net Gains and Losses Worksheet spells as its line 4, "Add lines 1, 2(j), and 3(d)", with the pointer "Enter this amount on line 5d" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8960.pdf, page 11). Read by /netInvestmentIncome as the line-5d term of Part I line 8.
THIS PATH USED TO BE LINE 5a AND 5d AT ONCE. While 5b and 5c were deferred the combine was an identity, so one fact carried both lines and its Name said so ("lines 5a/5d"). Once the two entry lines landed the identity stopped holding and the prose would have been false, so the line-5a expression moved UNCHANGED to /niitLine5aNetGainFromDisposition and this path became the combine it is named for. THAT SPLIT MOVED NO DOLLAR — 5b and 5c are $0 on every committed scenario, so line 5d equalled line 5a exactly as before.
A SECOND LANDING THE SAME DAY DID MOVE A DOLLAR, and this paragraph exists so the sentence above is not read as covering it. The per-term floor on line 5a's Schedule 1 line-4 (Form 4797 ordinary) term was removed, and the printed exclusion it stood in for — worksheet rows 2(a)/2(b) column (B) — was built as intakes feeding line 5b. One committed scenario changes: a return whose Form 4797 line 18 is -840.00 takes line 5a and this line 5d from 0.00 to -840.00, and its /netInvestmentIncome is unmoved. No other resolved row in the corpus moves, since that return is the only committed case whose /form4797OrdinaryIncome is negative.
SIGNED, ROUNDED, NEVER FLOORED. All three addends may be negative and the combine may be negative; /netInvestmentIncome (line 12) applies the single floor the form prints, so a negative line 5d offsets other investment income without ever driving NIIT below zero. Round at this line, as the pre-split fact already did.
COMPLETE FOR EVERY RETURN by construction: line 5a is complete-safe on both its terms and both new addends are complete-safe aliases with a True fallback.

Fact.Name: Net passive income for NIIT (Form 8960 line 4c, §469-passive portion, net of allowed losses), complete-safe
Fact.Description: Form 8960 line 4c "net income or loss" — the §1411 net investment income from the rental / passthrough / estate-trust activities of Schedule E, computed as the §469 PASSIVE net income (income NET of the currently-allowed passive losses). THIS KEYS on scheduleE:/passiveIncomeTotal − /passiveAllowedLossTotal — the pool's positive §469 passive income (active-participation rental + non-active rental + passive partnership/S-corp K-1 + passive estate/trust K-1, each already at-risk-limited) LESS the passive loss allowed this year under §469(d)(1) (income offset) and §469(i) (the active-rental special allowance). This is the exact "net passive contribution to total income" that scheduleE:/passiveAllowedLossTotal's own Description names, and equals the §469-passive portion of Schedule 1 line 5. §1411(c)(2) / the Form 8960 line 4b adjustment: income from a trade or business the taxpayer MATERIALLY PARTICIPATES in is NOT NII, so it is EXCLUDED here — /passiveIncomeTotal already omits the nonpassive materially-participated K-1/estate income (it flows through Schedule E Parts II/III line 32/37) AND the self-rental income recharacterized nonpassive under §469 (Reg. §1.469-2(f)(6); it flows through /rentalNonpassiveNet). NOTE on the self-rental §1411 authority: a rental activity is passive for NII "regardless of whether you materially participate" (i8960), so the §1411 exclusion of the self-rental PROFIT rests not on §469 recharacterization alone but on Reg. §1.1411-4(g)(6), which deems self-charged rental income treated as nonpassive under §1.469-2(f)(6) to be derived in the ordinary course of a trade/business and therefore NOT NII (§1411(c)(1)(A)(i) "other than … income derived in the ordinary course of a trade or business"). This is the §1411(c)(2) proof: a materially-participated-only return contributes 0 here. THE PRIOR BODY used /passiveIncomeTotal — the GROSS positive passive income — and called that "conservative (never under-computes)". It was conservative FOR THE FISC and it OVERCHARGED THE TAXPAYER: the gross positive income is ≥ the §469-net, so whenever a passive loss elsewhere in the pool is absorbed under §469(d)(1) the un-netted gross OVER-states line 4c, over-stating NII and over-charging NIIT ($30,000 non-active rental income absorbing a $10,000 passive K-1 loss → correct 4c $20,000, old model $30,000 → $10,000 NII overstatement → $380 over-tax at 3.8%). "Conservative" is a direction PLUS a beneficiary; the beneficiary here was the government, not the filer. Now netted, SIGNED: line 4c = /passiveIncomeTotal − /passiveAllowedLossTotal (Form 8960 line 4c is "net income OR LOSS"). The subtraction drops the gross income by the passive loss absorbed under §469(d)(1) (defect-2's target — net ≥ 0 there). It goes NEGATIVE only in the §469(i) special-allowance case (an active-participation rental loss allowed beyond pool passive income); that loss correctly reduces NII because an active-participation rental is PASSIVE for §1411 (i8960) and line 4b removes only the NONPASSIVE portion. An earlier draft floored this at 0 (GreaterOf); fg-reviewer M1 showed that re-committed the anti-pattern — a taxpayer- adverse "conservative for the fisc" floor — so it was removed. NII floors once, at line 12, so a net passive loss never drives NIIT below 0. interpretation:provisional (the signed line-4c reading is author-written, pinned by the node tests below — the positive-net absorbed-loss case AND the negative- net special-allowance case that reduces NII). Note: /rentalOverallPassiveNet was considered as the ready fix, but that fact is RENTAL-ONLY (rentalActive + rentalNonActive) and would return $30,000 for this own K-1 worked example — it omits the /k1PassiveNet loss; the pool-wide net used here is what nets the cross-activity loss. A PRIOR PARAGRAPH here said portfolio ROYALTY income was "DEFERRED (kept in the NIIT-interest guard, NOT freed)". It is not: /royaltyNetInvestmentIncome computes it as a SEPARATE line-4a component of line 4c, deliberately NOT inside this fact, because a portfolio royalty is not §469-passive and this fact's whole subject is the §469 passive net. Form 8960 line 3 non-qualified annuities remain un-computed and have no live enterable path. The NIIT-interest guard is retired.

Fact.Name: Portfolio royalty net investment income (the Form 8960 line 4a royalty component, surviving into line 4c)
Fact.Description:
The net royalty income on Schedule E line 26 — scheduleE:/royaltyNetIncome — as a component of Form 8960 line 4a.
WHICH LINE, AND WHY IT IS NOT 4c's PASSIVE FACT. Line 4a is "Rental real estate, royalties, partnerships, S corporations, trusts, trades or businesses, etc.", i.e. Schedule 1 line 5, and royalties are named on its face. Line 4b removes only net income derived in the ordinary course of a NON-section-1411 trade or business; a portfolio royalty is not a trade or business at all, so it survives line 4b untouched, and line 4c ("Combine lines 4a and 4b") carries it into line 8. This dictionary does not model lines 4a and 4b separately: it computes line 4c as the SUM OF TWO MODELLED COMPONENTS — /netPassiveIncomeForNiit (the §469 passive net) and this fact (the portfolio royalty net) — each added to line 8 in its own term. Putting the royalty inside /netPassiveIncomeForNiit would say a portfolio amount is §469-passive, which it is not.
NO DOUBLE COUNT, verified against the bodies rather than the comments: scheduleE: /passiveIncomeTotal is Round(Add(...)) over FIVE floored terms — GreaterOf(/rentalActiveNet, $0), GreaterOf(/rentalNonActiveNet, $0), GreaterOf(/k1PassiveNet, $0), GreaterOf(/estatePassiveNet, $0) and GreaterOf(/farmRentalPassiveNet, $0), at scheduleE.xml:10228-10252 — and not one of them is a royalty term, so /netPassiveIncomeForNiit and this fact are disjoint.
A PRIOR DESCRIPTION HERE MISQUOTED THIS BODY as a four-term Add of bare Dependencies: it omitted /farmRentalPassiveNet and it omitted the per-term GreaterOf floors. /farmRentalPassiveNet was present in the base tree, so that was a misquote and not a race. THE CONCLUSION IS UNAFFECTED — there is still no royalty term, and /netPassiveIncomeForNiit = /passiveIncomeTotal minus /passiveAllowedLossTotal carries none either — but the sentence's whole selling point is that it QUOTES the body, so quoting it wrongly is the defect regardless of where the conclusion landed.
SIGNED, NOT FLOORED, matching /netPassiveIncomeForNiit. Line 4a is "net income or loss" and net investment income is floored ONCE, at line 12. Today scheduleE:/knockoutRoyaltyActivityLoss refuses a negative royalty activity net, so this fact is non-negative on every fileable return; when that guard fills, a royalty LOSS will reduce net investment income here rather than being suppressed — which is the §1411(c)(1) treatment and the direction the fix "conservative for the fisc" finding rejected.
THE WORKING-INTEREST ARM COSTS NOTHING: an oil or gas working interest is a trade or business routed to Schedule C, and scheduleE:/royaltyNetIncome is $0 for it by its own fork, so no trade-or-business royalty reaches line 4a through this term.
Complete-safe: scheduleE:/royaltyNetIncome is itself complete-safe $0 when no royalty is claimed, and the IsComplete arm is FIRST so an unanswered royalty section resolves $0 rather than failing to resolve.

Fact.Name: Dividend reports attributed to the primary filer, for the NRA-spouse separate-NII computation
Fact.Description: Filter(dividendReports:/dividendReports, belongsToPrimaryFiler) — the same Filter-then-CollectionSum idiom interest.xml already ships for /primaryFilerInterestReports, applied here because dividendReports.xml carries the owner field (/dividendReports/*/filer, /dividendReports/*/belongsToPrimaryFiler) but no per-filer aggregate of its own (a named gap). Fact.Description: CollectionSum(/niitPrimaryFilerDividendReports/*/ordinaryDividends) — but ONLY when every dividend report on the return has an answered filer. dividendReports.xml deliberately carries no Placeholder on /dividendReports/*/filer (an unanswered report is NOT defaulted to the primary filer, unlike interest and 1099-R), so a report with no filer answer cannot be safely attributed to either spouse; this fact resolves INCOMPLETE rather than silently excluding or silently including that report's dividends. Fact.Name: The citizen/resident spouse's own separately-figured net investment income under the section 6013(g)/(h) NRA-spouse election without the NIIT-purposes box (fgv FED-8960-NRA-THRESHOLD-001, NII half)
Fact.Description:
Form 8960 Part I line 8, for a US citizen or resident who elected section 6013(g)/(h) to file jointly with an NRA spouse but did NOT also check the Form 8960 Part I NIIT-purposes election box (/niitFilingJointlyUnderNraSpouseElection true, /niitAppliesSection6013ElectionForNiitPurposes false — exactly the population /niitThreshold already swaps to the $125,000 MFS threshold for): "The U.S. citizen or resident spouse figures his or her NII ... separately" (i8960 line 128). This fact figures the PRIMARY filer's own NII, which is the citizen or resident spouse's unless filers:/writableSection6013ElectionNonresidentSpouse names the primary filer as the nonresident spouse; on that answer Form 8960 line 8 reads the secondary-filer twin /niitSecondaryFilerSeparateNiiForNraSpouseElection instead, through /niitCitizenSpouseSeparateNiiForNraSpouseElection, and this fact is not read.
BUILT FROM THE THREE COMPONENTS THAT CARRY A PER-FILER OWNER: interest (interest:/primaryFilerInterestTotal, an existing per-filer aggregate), ordinary dividends (/niitPrimaryFilerOrdinaryDividendsForNraSpouseElection, built this pass over dividendReports.xml's existing owner field), and 1099-R code-D annuities (/niitPrimaryFilerLine3AnnuitiesFromCodeD, built this pass over form1099Rs.xml's existing per-filer aggregate). NOT $0 ON AN ORDINARY RETURN: complete-safe false on the gate means this fact resolves $0 for every return outside the population, so it changes nothing outside its own gate.
UNATTRIBUTABLE-COMPONENT-PRESENT IS INCOMPLETE, not silently dropped or silently joint. Every OTHER component /niitLine8TotalInvestmentIncome's ordinary seven-term combine can carry has no per-filer split anywhere in this dictionary: capital gains/losses (scheduleD — 0 owner-field hits anywhere, the largest of the four collections this fill measured), section 469 passive and portfolio royalty income (/netPassiveIncomeForNiit, /royaltyNetInvestmentIncome — scheduleE has no per-filer split either), a section 475(e)(2) trader's Schedule C profit (/niitSection475eTraderScheduleCProfit), the line-6 CFC/PFIC adjustments, the line-7 other modifications, the return-level line-3 annuity writable (as opposed to its 1099-R code-D leg, which IS attributable and is included above), and any Part II investment expense or line-10 modification. If ANY of those is present (answered and nonzero) on a return in this population, this fact resolves INCOMPLETE rather than silently defaulting to the joint figure or excluding the unattributable amount — a disclosed data-completeness residue, not a favourable default. Likewise, a dividend report with an unanswered filer makes /niitPrimaryFilerOrdinaryDividendsForNraSpouseElection itself Incomplete, which propagates here the same way.
WIRED INTO /niitLine8TotalInvestmentIncome, not export-only: this fact REPLACES the ordinary seven-term combine for the gated population (see that fact's Description), which in turn improves /netInvestmentIncome and /netInvestmentIncomeTax for this population — a DISCLOSED MIXED STATE, not a fully correct answer: NII is now separately figured, but /niitMagi still reads the JOINT return's AGI (the MAGI split is not built). No committed scenario answers this population's gate (grepped this pass), so this wiring is additive-clean: value-identical on every scenario in the corpus.

Fact.Name: A net investment income component with no per-filer owner is present on the return
Fact.Description: TRUE when any Form 8960 Part I or Part II component that this dictionary cannot attribute to one spouse is answered and nonzero: section 469 passive income, royalty net investment income, a section 475(e)(2) trader's Schedule C profit, net capital gain, the line 6 CFC and PFIC adjustments, the line 7 other modifications, the Part II line 11 total, or the return-level line 3 annuities writable (its 1099-R code D leg IS attributable and is not tested here). One list, read by both the primary-filer and the secondary-filer separate figures, so the two can never test different components.

Fact.Description:
Form 8960 Part I line 8 for the citizen or resident spouse when that spouse is the SECONDARY filer: the return's joint filing status rests on the section 6013(g) or 6013(h) election, the Form 8960 box applying it for NIIT purposes is not checked, and filers:/section6013ElectionNonresidentSpouseIsPrimaryFilerOnly says the nonresident spouse is the primary filer. Fact.Name: The citizen or resident spouse's own separately figured net investment income under the section 6013(g) or 6013(h) election
Fact.Description: Picks the spouse whose own net investment income Form 8960 line 8 carries when the election is not applied for NIIT purposes. filers:/writableSection6013ElectionNonresidentSpouse names the nonresident spouse: answered primaryFiler, the citizen or resident spouse is the secondary filer and this reads /niitSecondaryFilerSeparateNiiForNraSpouseElection; answered secondaryFiler or unanswered, it reads /niitPrimaryFilerSeparateNiiForNraSpouseElection as before the question existed; answered bothFilers, neither spouse was a citizen or resident for the whole year, each is a dual-status individual whose section 1411 figures cover only the resident part of the year, nothing here apportions that, and this resolves INCOMPLETE. Fact.Name: Form 8960 Part I line 8, total investment income (the signed combine of lines 1, 2, 3, 4c, 5d, 6 and 7)
Fact.Description:
Form 8960 Part I line 8, "Total investment income. Combine lines 1, 2, 3, 4c, 5d, 6, and 7". Minted by the stranded results reconciliation, because until this build ONE fact (/netInvestmentIncome) carried BOTH printed boxes, line 8 and line 12. That was sound only while Part II was structurally $0: line 12 is "Subtract Part II, line 11, from Part I, line 8", so the moment line 11 can be non zero the two boxes hold different numbers and one fact cannot print both. This fact is line 8; /netInvestmentIncome is line 12 and now reads this minus line 11.
SIGNED, NOT FLOORED. The printed line 8 says "Combine" and carries no "if zero or less, enter -0-" clause; the single floor the form prints is on line 12, and /netInvestmentIncome applies it. A negative line 5d or a negative line 4c therefore offsets other investment income here exactly as the form intends, and can never drive the tax below zero.
SEVEN TERMS, ONE READING PER PRINTED BOX. Each addend is the fact the register already prints in that box, so the printed line 8 cannot disagree with the printed lines above it: line 1 /niitLine1TaxableInterest, line 2 /niitLine2OrdinaryDividends, line 3 /niitLine3Annuities, line 4c /niitLine4cRentalRoyaltyAndPassthroughTotal, line 5d /netCapitalGainForNiit, line 6 /niitLine6CfcAndPficAdjustments, line 7 /niitLine7OtherModifications.
LINE 4c REPLACES TWO TERMS, IT DOES NOT JOIN THEM. The superseded body added the two modelled line 4a components (/royaltyNetInvestmentIncome and /netPassiveIncomeForNiit) directly. /niitLine4cRentalRoyaltyAndPassthroughTotal is exactly those two — it does NOT also read /niitLine4bNonSection1411Adjustment (see that fact's Description for why a 4b term would double-subtract) — so swapping the pair for the 4c total is value identical on every return, answered or unanswered line 4b alike. Adding 4c alongside the pair would have double counted line 4a.
COMPLETE FOR EVERY RETURN. Lines 1 and 2 are direct aliases of two facts that are themselves complete safe; lines 3, 4b, 6 and 7 are IsComplete guarded intakes with a $0 fallback; line 5d is complete safe by construction (see /netCapitalGainForNiit). So this fact and every consumer of it keep the completeness /line21OfSchedule2 has always had.
NRA-SPOUSE SEPARATE-NII OVERRIDE: for a filer whose MFJ status rests on the section 6013(g)/(h) NRA-spouse election without the NIIT-purposes box, this line reads /niitCitizenSpouseSeparateNiiForNraSpouseElection (the primary or the secondary filer's own separate NII, whichever spouse is the citizen or resident) instead of the ordinary seven-term combine (see that fact's Description for the full account, including the Incomplete residue when an unattributable component is present). No committed scenario answers that gate, so the seven-term combine below — the True fallback — is the ONLY arm any committed scenario exercises, and is unchanged.

Fact.Name: Net investment income (Form 8960 line 12: Part I line 8 less Part II line 11, floored at $0)
Fact.Description:
Form 8960 Part III line 12, "Net investment income. Subtract Part II, line 11, from Part I, line 8 ... If zero or less, enter -0-": /niitLine8TotalInvestmentIncome less /niitLine11TotalDeductionsAndModifications, floored at $0. This is the base of /niitLine16SmallerOfNetInvestmentIncomeOrMagiExcess and of /netInvestmentIncomeTax, which is why the whole of Part II now changes the tax.
REBUILT (stranded results reconciliation). THE SUPERSEDED BODY WAS THE LINE 8 COMBINE WITH FOUR PRINTED TERMS MISSING AND PART II NOT SUBTRACTED AT ALL: it added /interestIncome, /ordinaryDividends, /netCapitalGainForNiit, /netPassiveIncomeForNiit and /royaltyNetInvestmentIncome, and it named itself "line 8 / line 12" because while Part II was out of scope the two boxes held one number. A return that entered a line 3 annuity, a line 4b non section 1411 adjustment, a line 6 CFC or PFIC adjustment, a line 7 other modification, or ANY Part II expense printed those boxes and its own line 12 ignored every one of them. DIRECTION OF THE ERROR: line 11 and the omitted terms were dropped, so net investment income and the 3.8 percent tax on it were OVERSTATED for any such return (understated only in the rarer case of a negative line 4b, 6 or 7 entry). Both boxes are now separately modelled: line 8 is /niitLine8TotalInvestmentIncome, the seven term signed combine, and this fact is line 12.
NO COMMITTED SCENARIO MOVES. Every new term is $0 unless a filer answers an intake that no committed scenario answers: lines 3, 4b, 6, 7, 9b, 9c and 10 are unanswered everywhere, line 9a is $0 for a standard deduction return and reads the same Form 4952 deduction it always did, and the line 4c swap is value identical while line 4b is unanswered (see /niitLine8TotalInvestmentIncome for why 4c REPLACES the two 4a components rather than joining them). The tags are left exactly as VERIFY wrote them, the precedent /netCapitalGainForNiit records for a checked-again pin.
REGISTER ITEM FOR THE LEAD: dictionary/pdf/2025/IRS8960/en/configuration.yml maps BOTH f1_15[0] (line 8) and f1_22[0] (line 12) to this fact. f1_15[0] must be repointed at /niitLine8TotalInvestmentIncome; f1_22[0] stays here. Until it is, a Part II return prints its line 12 value in the line 8 box.
All three now arrive through /niitLine4cRentalRoyaltyAndPassthroughTotal and /netCapitalGainForNiit.

Fact.Name: Form 8960 line 13 / MAGI Worksheet line 2(c) — the section 911 add-back
Fact.Description:
MAGI Worksheet line 2(c) = Form 2555 line 42 − Form 2555 line 44, floored at zero, and $0 whenever form2555 /filesForm2555ForeignEarnedIncomeExclusion is false. The Form 8960 instructions give this line twice, once in prose and once as arithmetic, and the arithmetic version is the one this fact encodes: "Section 911. If you exclude amounts from income under section 911, to calculate your MAGI, you must increase your AGI by the excess of the amount excluded from income under section 911(a)(1) over the amount of any deductions (taken into account in computing AGI) or exclusions disallowed under section 911(d)(6) for the amount excluded from income under section 911(a)(1)" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8960.pdf, page 22), followed by "Use the Line 13—MAGI Worksheet in these instructions to compute your MAGI" (lines 1412-1413).
THE SUBTRAHEND HAS A PATH AFTER ALL, AND THIS IS THE FINDING THAT UNBLOCKED THE NODE. The printed Line 13—MAGI Worksheet names the amount outright: line "2(a) Enter your foreign earned income exclusion (from line 42 of Form 2555)", line "2(b) Enter the deductions reported on line 44 of Form 2555 allocable to your foreign earned income exclusion" — printed inside parentheses, i.e. subtracted — and line "2(c) Combine lines 2(a) and 2(b)" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8960.pdf, page 23). Form 2555 line 44 is form2555 /form2555Line44DeductionsAllocableToExcludedIncome, SHIPPING. So no new writable is minted here and no new question is asked: both terms are already-collected Form 2555 entries.
THE FLOOR IS THE PROSE WINNING OVER THE WORKSHEET, deliberately and in the conservative direction. Worksheet line 2(c) says "Combine", with no "if zero or less, enter -0-"; the narrative says "the EXCESS of the amount excluded ... over the amount of any deductions", which is a floored subtraction. Unfloored, a filer whose Form 2555 line 44 exceeds their line 42 would carry a NEGATIVE line 2(c) and a MAGI BELOW their AGI, cutting their NIIT below what a filer with no exclusion at all would owe — an unfloored reading that no sentence in the instructions asks for. Flooring can only raise MAGI, which is the taxpayer-adverse and therefore World-1-safe direction. Both arms are witnessed one dollar apart by tests/nodes/ty2025/form8960/niit-magi-911-addback-line44-below-exclusion (line 44 = 99,999, add-back +1) and -line44-exceeds-exclusion (line 44 = 100,001, add-back 0 rather than −1).
SECTION 911(a)(1) ALONE — never line 43, never the possession exclusions. The instruction names section 911(a)(1) twice in one sentence, so the term is form2555 /foreignEarnedIncomeExclusion911 (Form 2555 line 42, WITHOUT the section 911(a)(2) housing exclusion at line 36) and not /form2555Line43Section911TotalExclusions. A section 931 or 933 possession exclusion is NOT added back on this line either: the instruction's opening sentence makes the complement plain — "If you didn't exclude any amounts from your gross income under section 911 and you don't own an interest in a CFC or PFIC, your MAGI is your AGI as reported on Form 1040 or 1040-SR" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8960.pdf, page 22). ctcOdc /possessionIncomeExclusion931 and /puertoRicoIncomeExclusion933 exist and this line reads neither.
GATED ON THE ATTESTATION, which is the add-back-without-exclusion discipline rather than belt-and-braces. form2555 /foreignEarnedIncomeExclusion911 is the complete-safe alias of the line-42 entry and is NOT itself gated; the two Schedule 1 legs that carry the exclusion OUT of AGI (form2555 /schedule1Line8dForeignEarnedIncomeExclusion and /schedule1Line24jHousingDeduction) ARE. Reading the amount ungated here would add back an exclusion that never reduced AGI for a filer who entered Form 2555 figures without answering the attestation. The gate makes the two sides agree by construction.
TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING: Dollar, integer cents, NON-NEGATIVE (the floor). No rounding at this node; MAGI rounds where it is assembled.
WORLD-1: byte-identical on the committed corpus. No scenario answers the attestation, so this fact is $0 everywhere today, and every return whose gate is false keeps MAGI = AGI, which is what the instruction's own opening sentence calls the ordinary case.

Fact.Name: An adjusted gross income or MAGI component of this return cannot be attributed to one spouse
Fact.Description:
True when any term of taxCalculations /agi, or of the Form 8960 Line 13-MAGI Worksheet, is present on this return and has no per-filer split anywhere in this dictionary. It is the completeness fence of /niitPrimaryFilerSeparateMagiForNraSpouseElection: a citizen or resident married to a nonresident alien figures MAGI separately from the joint return, and a component that nobody can attribute to one spouse must leave that separate MAGI INCOMPLETE rather than be silently taken whole, silently dropped, or replaced by the joint figure.
THE TERMS THAT ARE ATTRIBUTABLE ARE NOT LISTED HERE, and that is the point of the split: Form 1040 line 1z through income /primaryFilerEmployerIncomeSubtotalBase, line 2b through interest /primaryFilerInterestTotal, line 3b through /niitPrimaryFilerOrdinaryDividendsForNraSpouseElection, Schedule 1 line 3 through scheduleC /primaryFilerScheduleCNetProfit, and on the deduction side the Schedule 1 line 15 half of self-employment tax and the line 20 IRA deduction, each of which already ships a primary-filer aggregate. Every OTHER term of the two sums is a conjunct below, INCLUDING the return-level residues of the four lines that are partly attributable: interest /primaryFilerInterestTotal states in its own Description that the boxes 10 to 12 adjustment, the Form 8815 exclusion, the Form 8958 allocation, the Schedule K-1 interest and the Schedule B line-1 subtractions are return-level and are not divided between the filers, so each of those is fenced here rather than assumed to be the primary filer's.
WHY EACH CONJUNCT IS A SEPARATE COMPARISON AGAINST ZERO rather than one reconciliation of the parts against the joint total. A reconciliation cancels: Form 1040 line 1z carries a NEGATIVE statutory-employee term and line 2b carries a negative Form 8815 exclusion and a negative Schedule B line-1 adjustment, so opposite-signed unattributed items can sum to zero while each one is misattributed. A per-term comparison has no such state.
EVERY CONJUNCT IS IsComplete-GUARDED, and the reason is a MEASURED engine behaviour rather than caution. Several of these terms sit in an untaken arm of an upstream Switch - the two original-issue-discount totals are the Schedule B and the no-Schedule-B arms of interest /interestIncome, and only one of them is ever evaluated - so a term can be INCOMPLETE on a return whose taxCalculations /agi is Complete, which means it contributes nothing to that return's adjusted gross income. The guard reads "PRESENT AND NONZERO", which is the test this fence is for.
WHAT STOPS THAT GUARD FROM SILENTLY DROPPING A REAL COMPONENT is the companion condition on the consuming fact: /niitPrimaryFilerSeparateMagiForNraSpouseElection requires taxCalculations /agi to be COMPLETE. A component that is present but unanswered makes /agi Incomplete, and the separate MAGI then refuses on that gate instead of on this one. The two conditions together are "AGI is settled, and nothing in it is unattributable".
DIRECTION AND COMPLETENESS. Every conjunct is complete-safe $0 on a return that does not report that item, so this fact is Complete FALSE on an ordinary return and /niitPrimaryFilerSeparateMagiForNraSpouseElection computes. The possession proration conjunct is a BOOLEAN rather than a dollar comparison: when 26 CFR 1.933-1(c) applies, taxCalculations /allowableAdjustmentsToIncome is a prorated fraction of the adjustments rather than their sum, and no per-filer form of that proration exists.

Fact.Name: The citizen or resident spouse's own modified adjusted gross income under a section 6013(g) or 6013(h) election that was not applied for NIIT purposes
Fact.Description:
Form 8960 line 13 for a United States citizen or resident who elected under section 6013(g) or 6013(h) to file a JOINT return with a nonresident alien spouse but did NOT also check the Form 8960 Part I box applying that election for NIIT purposes: that filer is treated as married filing separately for section 1411 and figures MAGI on the filer's OWN items, not on the joint return's. The population is exactly the one /niitThreshold's first Case already swaps to the $125,000 threshold for and /niitPrimaryFilerSeparateNiiForNraSpouseElection already figures net investment income for; this fact is the MAGI half of that pair.
EVERY COMPONENT BELOW IS A PRIMARY-FILER AGGREGATE. The primary filer is the citizen or resident spouse unless filers:/writableSection6013ElectionNonresidentSpouse names the primary filer as the nonresident spouse; on that answer line 13 reads the secondary-filer twin /niitSecondaryFilerSeparateMagiForNraSpouseElection instead, through /niitCitizenSpouseSeparateMagiForNraSpouseElection, and this fact is not read.
THE BODY IS IRC 62(a) ON THE PRIMARY FILER'S OWN PARTS: the primary filer's Form 1040 line 1z base, line 2b taxable interest, line 3b ordinary dividends and Schedule 1 line 3 Schedule C net profit, less that filer's own half of self-employment tax and that filer's own traditional IRA deduction (including the section 219(f)(6) prior-year excess leg). The rounding mirrors taxCalculations /agi exactly - one Round over the income side, then one Round over the subtraction - so the two are comparable cent for cent.
NO MAGI ADD-BACK IS ADDED, and that is a fenced conclusion rather than an omission. The Line 13-MAGI Worksheet adds the section 911 exclusion, the Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) box 14 code H adjustment and the CFC/QEF reconciliation. form2555 states in its own module that it has no per-filer Form 2555 - the four entries are per RETURN - and the other two are return-level as well, so all three are conjuncts of /niitNraSpouseElectionUnattributedAgiComponentPresent: when any of them is nonzero this fact is INCOMPLETE, and when none is, MAGI equals the primary filer's own AGI.
TAXCALCULATIONS /agi MUST BE COMPLETE, and that conjunct is what makes the fence sound rather than merely present. Each conjunct of /niitNraSpouseElectionUnattributedAgiComponentPresent asks whether a term is PRESENT AND NONZERO, so an unanswered term reads as absent there; requiring a Complete /agi here is what forecloses the case where the term really was present and simply unanswered, because such a term makes /agi Incomplete and this Case then never matches.
UNATTRIBUTABLE-COMPONENT-PRESENT IS INCOMPLETE, never joint and never dropped. Every term of /agi with no per-filer split - taxable IRA and pension distributions, taxable social security, capital gains, Schedule 1 other income, Schedule E, alimony, Form 4797, Schedule F, the Form 8958 community-property allocations, the return-level interest and dividend residues and every Schedule 1 Part II adjustment other than the two named above - is a conjunct of that fence. The Switch has NO True catch-all: a return in the population that trips the fence runs off the end and resolves Incomplete, which is what refuses the line 13 entry instead of printing an unproven one.
OUTSIDE THE POPULATION THIS IS A COMPLETE $0 and is never read: /niitMagi consults it only on the same gate, so every other return keeps the joint Line 13-MAGI Worksheet sum unchanged.
WHAT THIS CORRECTS. Before this fact, Form 8960 line 13 for this population was the JOINT MAGI, which counts the nonresident spouse's income against a $125,000 threshold and inflates the line 15 excess. TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING: Dollar, integer cents. No floor: AGI itself may be negative.

Fact.Name: The secondary filer's own modified adjusted gross income, when the section 6013(g) or 6013(h) election names the primary filer as the nonresident spouse
Fact.Description:
Form 8960 line 13 for the citizen or resident spouse when that spouse is the SECONDARY filer. The secondary-filer twin of /niitPrimaryFilerSeparateMagiForNraSpouseElection, term for term: the secondary filer's own Form 1040 line 1z base, line 2b taxable interest, line 3b ordinary dividends and Schedule 1 line 3 Schedule C net profit, less that filer's own half of self-employment tax and own traditional IRA deduction. The section 219(f)(6) prior-year excess leg is a primary-filer fact only in this dictionary, so it has no secondary term here: a deduction this dictionary never gives the secondary filer is not in the joint adjusted gross income on that filer's behalf either. Rounded exactly as the twin and taxCalculations /agi round.
THE SAME FENCE AS THE TWIN, unchanged: /niitNraSpouseElectionUnattributedAgiComponentPresent lists every adjusted gross income or MAGI-worksheet term that has no per-filer split, and it is return-level, so it fences either spouse's figure equally. A Complete /agi is required for the reason the twin states. The Switch has no catch-all: inside the population a fenced return runs off the end and resolves INCOMPLETE. Outside it, a complete $0 nothing reads.

Fact.Name: The citizen or resident spouse's own modified adjusted gross income under the section 6013(g) or 6013(h) election
Fact.Description: Picks the spouse whose own MAGI Form 8960 line 13 carries when the election is not applied for NIIT purposes, on exactly the three arms /niitCitizenSpouseSeparateNiiForNraSpouseElection uses, so line 8 and line 13 always describe the same spouse: the nonresident spouse named as the primary filer reads /niitSecondaryFilerSeparateMagiForNraSpouseElection; named as the secondary filer, or unanswered, reads /niitPrimaryFilerSeparateMagiForNraSpouseElection; both spouses dual-status resolves INCOMPLETE.

Fact.Name: Other CFC and PFIC adjustments to MAGI (Line 13 MAGI Worksheet line 3)
Fact.Description: The total of the Line 13 MAGI Worksheet line 3 adjustments not asked elsewhere: the increase for excess distributions from a section 1291 fund that are dividends, or gain treated as an excess distribution, included in MAGI but not in gross income for regular tax; the increase or decrease for an adjustment to gain or loss on the disposition of a CFC or QEF, or of a partnership or S corporation interest that holds one; and the increase or decrease for an investment interest adjustment under Regulations section 1.1411-10(c)(5). Enter a decrease as a negative number. Do not include the CFC and QEF inclusions and distributions reported per holding, or the Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) box 14 code H amount. The amount is one return-level figure: on a joint return under a section 6013(g) or 6013(h) election that does not apply the election for NIIT purposes, a nonzero amount cannot be attributed to the citizen or resident spouse, so /niitNraSpouseElectionUnattributedAgiComponentPresent leaves that spouse's separate MAGI Incomplete rather than dropping it.

Fact.Name: Other CFC and PFIC adjustments to MAGI, complete-safe
Fact.Description: The filer's signed total of the remaining Line 13 MAGI Worksheet line 3 adjustments; $0 when unanswered.

Fact.Name: Form 8960 line 13 — modified adjusted gross income
Fact.Description:
Form 8960 line 13 = Line 13—MAGI Worksheet line 4, "Enter the sum of line 1, line 2(c), and line 3" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8960.pdf, page 23) — worksheet line 1 is taxCalculations /agi, line 2(c) is /niitMagiForeignEarnedIncomeAddback above, and worksheet line 3 ("Adjustments for certain CFCs and certain PFICs") carries ONE modelled term: the box 14 code H bullet the worksheet's own line-3 list ends on ("Increase or decrease AGI ... by the amount reported to you in box 14, code H, of Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) that requires a MAGI adjustment", sources/i8960-ty2025-2026-07.xml line 1548) — /niitEstateTrustK1Box14CodeHMagiAdjustment, floored to the positive-amount case the instruction states unconditionally. Nothing in this dictionary models a CFC, a PFIC, a QEF election, Form 5471 or Form 8621, and the module header records line 6 CFC/PFIC income as deferred for the same reason, so every OTHER worksheet line 3 bullet (the CFC/PFIC inclusion, exclusion and disposition adjustments) are carried by the terms named below.
WHY THIS IS A NAMED FACT rather than an expression inside /netInvestmentIncomeTax: Form 8960 line 13 is a printed entry line, and until this fill the module comment's "line 13 = MAGI (= /agi; no §911/§1.1411 add-backs in scope)" was the only place the identity lived. MAGI and AGI are now different numbers for a Form 2555 filer, and the difference is the thing the node tests pin.
COMPLETENESS AND PROVISIONALITY ARE PRESERVED BY CONSTRUCTION. /niitMagiForeignEarnedIncomeAddback is total, so /niitMagi carries the status of /agi. The line-15 arithmetic and line-17 tax now pass that status through: an unresolved AGI remains Incomplete, while a provisional AGI remains Placeholder with its provisional arithmetic value.
TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING: Dollar, integer cents. No floor — AGI itself may be negative and the add-back cannot pull MAGI below AGI.
MAGI WORKSHEET LINE 3 NOW CARRIES A SECOND TERM: /niitCfcQefMagiAdjustment, the per-holding CFC/QEF reconciliation. For a holding with no section 1.1411-10(g) election it subtracts the current section 951(a)/951A/1293(a) inclusions and adds the chapter-1-excluded distribution included in NII; for an elected holding it adds only the distribution, because the election keeps the inclusions in MAGI. Signed, so MAGI may now fall below AGI. The term is $0 on every return with no answered holding.
MAGI WORKSHEET LINE 3 CARRIES A THIRD TERM: /niitMagiWorksheetLine3OtherAdjustments, the filer's signed total of the remaining line-3 bullets (section 1291 excess distributions and gain included in MAGI but not in gross income, the disposition adjustments, the section 1.1411-10(c)(5) investment-interest adjustment), $0 when unanswered.
LINE 13 IS NO LONGER ALWAYS THE JOINT WORKSHEET SUM.
