On a return whose married-filing-jointly status rests on the section 6013(g) or 6013(h) nonresident alien spouse election and that did NOT also check the Form 8960 Part I box applying that election for NIIT purposes, this line is the CITIZEN OR RESIDENT SPOUSE'S OWN MAGI - /niitCitizenSpouseSeparateMagiForNraSpouseElection, the primary or the secondary filer's own figure according to filers:/writableSection6013ElectionNonresidentSpouse - because that filer is treated as married filing separately for section 1411 and figures MAGI separately. The gate is the same pair of complete-safe booleans /niitThreshold's first Case already tests, so the printed line 13 and the line 14 threshold always describe the same population.
THE COMPLETENESS SENTENCE ABOVE IS NARROWED BY THAT CASE. "Carries the status of /agi" is true on every return outside that population and on no return inside it: the separate MAGI resolves Incomplete whenever an AGI or MAGI-worksheet component of the return has no per-filer split, so line 13 can now be Incomplete while /agi is Complete. That is the intended direction - it refuses the line rather than printing the joint figure, which over-states this filer's excess over the $125,000 threshold.

Fact.Name: Section 1411(e)(1) — NIIT does not apply to a primary filer who is a nonresident alien for the whole year
Fact.Description:
True when the primary filer is NOT a resident for chapter 1 purposes (filers:/primaryFilerIsResidentForChapter1 false) on a return with any net investment income to tax, so the whole of Form 8960 Part III — and the tax it produces — does not apply, per section 1411(e)(1): "This section shall not apply to— (1) a nonresident alien." MOOT (Complete, false) on a return with no net investment income at all (/niitLine8TotalInvestmentIncome at or below $0): the exclusion changes nothing there regardless of residency, so it never introduces incompleteness on an immaterial return. UNANSWERED RESIDENCY ON A RETURN WITH NET INVESTMENT INCOME IS INCOMPLETE, never a silent default either way — reads filers:/primaryFilerIsResidentForChapter1 directly rather than re-deriving residency, and that fact is itself Incomplete on an unanswered attestation by its own construction, which is what propagates here.
THIS EXCLUSION IS NARROWER THAN THE POPULATION THE CONTRACT NAMED. This dictionary's own submission gate already refuses a whole-year NRA primary filer outright — flow:/flowIsKnockedOut reads filers:/primaryFilerResidencyKnockout with BlockSubmissionOnTrue, so a return this fact would exclude can never be SUBMITTED in the first place. This fact still matters during the interview, before that knockout is surfaced, so it is not vacuous; it is also why building it changes no committed scenario (every submittable scenario already answers residency). NARROWED, not built here: (1) the DUAL-STATUS apportionment (i8960 lines 105-112) — a resident for only PART of the year owes NIIT for that part only, on an unprorated threshold, which needs a residency-period slicing mechanism this dictionary has for no fact, not only this one; (2) the missing SECONDARY filer twin — no filers:/secondaryFilerIsResidentForChapter1 exists (only the three raw, unconsolidated /secondaryFiler/* attestations do), so a secondary filer's own whole-year NRA status cannot be tested the same way the primary filer's can; building that twin is filers.xml work, outside this unit's grant; (3) the population that twin would serve — a secondary filer attesting NRA-for-the-whole-year with NO section 6013(g)/(h) election in place — is not a valid Form 1040 at all (the dictionary's own convention, per form1040:/form1040NonresidentAlienSpouseElectionName, is that the NRA spouse under a 6013(g)/(h) election is always the SECONDARY filer; absent that election an NRA spouse has no basis to appear as a joint-return secondary filer). The correct fix for (3) is a filers-side refusal naming that malformed-return residue, not a Form 8960 exclusion computing on a return that should not exist — named here as the residue this build does not reach, not built.

Fact.Name: Knockout: the separately figured NIIT of a citizen or resident married to a nonresident alien cannot be decided
Fact.Description:
SCREEN TEXT: "You elected to file jointly with a spouse who was a nonresident alien, and you did not also apply that election for the net investment income tax. For that tax you must figure your own net investment income and modified adjusted gross income separately from your spouse's. Your return has income or adjustments we can't yet split between the two of you (or both of you were nonresident aliens for part of the year), so we can't file this return."
Blocks submission when the return's joint filing status rests on the section 6013(g) or 6013(h) election (/niitFilingJointlyUnderNraSpouseElection), the Form 8960 box applying that election for NIIT purposes is not checked (/niitAppliesSection6013ElectionForNiitPurposes false), and ANY of: both spouses began the year as nonresident aliens (filers:/section6013ElectionBothSpousesNonresidentPartOfYear, a dual-status year for each, which nothing here apportions); a net investment income component with no per-filer owner is present (/niitNraSpouseElectionUnattributedNiiComponentPresent); an adjusted gross income or Line 13 MAGI component with no per-filer split is present (/niitNraSpouseElectionUnattributedAgiComponentPresent). Each of those leaves the citizen or resident spouse's separate Form 8960 line 8 or line 13 undecidable; this refusal states the reason instead of leaving the tax unresolved. Complete-safe: FALSE on every return outside the section 6013(g)/(h) election without the NIIT box.

Fact.Name: A section 1296 PFIC position needs the first-year excess-distribution coordination
Fact.Description: TRUE when the answered /niitSection1296Positions collection holds a position with the mark-to-market election in effect (../writableMarketableStockElectionApplies) that also answers that the section 1296(j) first-year coordination applies (../writableRequiresFirstYearCoordination). That year's mark is a section 1291 excess distribution computation, which this dictionary does not perform. Complete-safe: FALSE when the collection is unanswered or no such position is recorded. Read by /knockoutNiitCfcPficAdjustmentNotModeled.

Fact.Name: A Form 8960 line 6 CFC or PFIC amount entered in a box that has no Line 13 MAGI companion
Fact.Description: TRUE when any of these line 6 intakes is answered and not $0: the section 1291 excess-distribution inclusion (/writableNiitLine6Section1291ExcessDistributionInclusion), the section 1.1411-10(g) election-in-place inclusion (/writableNiitLine6CfcQefElectionInPlaceInclusion), the no-election adjustment (/writableNiitLine6CfcQefNoElectionAdjustment), or the residual line 6 box (/writableNiitLine6CfcAndPficAdjustments). Each changes Form 8960 line 6 while nothing changes line 13: the Line 13 instructions increase AGI for section 1291 excess distributions and decrease or increase it for CFC and QEF inclusions and distributions, and /niitMagi reads only the per-holding /niitCfcQefMagiAdjustment. These boxes also carry none of the disposition, basis or investment-interest exclusions the per-holding /niitCfcQefHoldings route asks the filer to confirm. The section 1296 mark-to-market box is not listed: a PFIC marked to market under section 1296 is excepted from the MAGI adjustments. Complete-safe: an unanswered box is not present. Read by /knockoutNiitCfcPficAdjustmentNotModeled.

Fact.Name: A CFC or QEF holding is answered as outside the annual reconciliation route
Fact.Description: TRUE when the answered /niitCfcQefHoldings collection holds a record whose ../writableAnnualScopeConfirmed is answered FALSE: the filer has said the holding involves something the per-holding route excludes, such as a direct or indirect disposition of the stock, a basis transfer, an investment interest expense adjustment, a holding in a section 1411 trade or business, or a pre-2014 transition case. Complete-safe: FALSE when the collection is unanswered or every record confirms the scope or leaves it blank (a blank leaves that record's figures Incomplete on its own). Read by /knockoutNiitCfcPficAdjustmentNotModeled.

Fact.Name: Knockout: a CFC or PFIC adjustment to net investment income or MAGI that is not figured
Fact.Description:
SCREEN TEXT: "Your return includes a controlled foreign corporation (CFC) or passive foreign investment company (PFIC) item whose effect on the net investment income tax we can't yet figure: a section 1291 excess distribution, a first-year mark-to-market election, a line 6 amount entered without the per-holding worksheet, or a holding with a sale, basis transfer, interest expense adjustment or trade or business use. We can't file this return."
Blocks submission when ANY of: a section 1296 position needs the section 1296(j) first-year coordination (/niitSection1296FirstYearCoordinationPresent); a line 6 amount sits in a box with no Line 13 MAGI companion (/niitLine6AmountWithoutMagiCompanionPresent); or a CFC or QEF holding is answered as outside the annual reconciliation route (/niitCfcQefHoldingOutsideAnnualScopePresent). What still computes: the section 1296 annual mark through /niitSection1296Positions or its manual box, and the per-holding CFC and QEF route through /niitCfcQefHoldings with its own MAGI adjustment. Complete-safe: FALSE on a return with none of those items.

Fact.Name: Net Investment Income Tax (Form 8960 line 17 → Schedule 2 line 12)
Fact.Description:
Form 8960 Part III line 17: 3.8% × the SMALLER of net investment income (line 12, /netInvestmentIncome) and the excess of MAGI over the threshold (line 15 = max(0, /niitMagi − /niitThreshold)). Flows to Schedule 2 (Form 1040) line 12, included in Schedule 2 line 21 (/line21OfSchedule2) → Form 1040 line 23 → total tax. 0 when there is no net investment income or MAGI is at/below the threshold (additive-clean regression). MAGI IS /niitMagi, not a bare /agi, because the Form 8960 line-13 section 911 add-back ships as /niitMagiForeignEarnedIncomeAddback and MAGI is no longer AGI for a Form 2555 filer. The two stay equal for every return whose form2555 gate is false, which is every committed scenario. MAGI that is unanswered or Placeholder now leaves this tax Incomplete; it can no longer print a silent $0 when the line-15 limitation cannot be figured. A complete zero line 12 or a complete nonresident-alien exclusion still proves $0 without needing the remaining inputs.
NRA EXCLUSION WRAPPER: section 1411(e)(1) means the NIIT "shall not apply" to a nonresident alien at all, so /niitNonresidentAlienExclusion gates the whole of the arithmetic below to $0 when true, rather than only zeroing one addend. When that exclusion fact is Incomplete (net investment income present, primary filer residency unanswered), this fact is Incomplete too — an unanswered condition of allowance, not a silent default. Every committed scenario answers residency, so this wrap is additive-clean: IsComplete(/niitNonresidentAlienExclusion) is true and its value is false on every one of them; the delegated line-17 computation below reads the same exclusion but preserves Placeholder and Incomplete arithmetic states.

Fact.Name: Form 8960 line 17 tax with no default for missing MAGI
Fact.Description: Net investment income tax for an individual: 3.8 percent of the smaller of line 12 and line 15, rounded to whole dollars. A complete zero on line 12 makes the tax zero without needing MAGI or residency. A complete nonresident-alien exclusion also makes the tax zero. A complete exclusion answer of false calculates from line 16 without an IsComplete fence, so a Placeholder line 12 or MAGI keeps its provisional tax as Placeholder and a genuinely Incomplete input leaves the tax Incomplete. When neither line 12 nor the exclusion is complete and line 12 is a provisional zero, the tax is that provisional zero (line 15 is floored at zero, so line 16 is zero whatever MAGI turns out to be): the result stays Placeholder, never a Complete zero. Every other state, including a line 12 amount to tax while primary-filer residency is unanswered, is Incomplete. There is no fallback $0 when MAGI is unavailable.

Fact.Name: Form 8960 line 17: line 12 or the nonresident-alien exclusion is complete
Fact.Description: True when Form 8960 line 12 (net investment income) is complete or the section 1411(e)(1) nonresident-alien exclusion is complete; false when both are still provisional or unanswered. Always complete. The line-17 tax reads it to recognise a return with no settled NIIT input, where a provisional zero line 12 stays a provisional zero tax.

Fact.Name: Form 8960 zero dollar floor
Fact.Description: The $0 constant Form 8960 line 15 floors against ("Subtract line 14 from line 13. If zero or less, enter -0-") and the else arm of the line 9a itemizing switch. The supported templates have no unary positive part and no zero literal inline in a Switch arm, so each module declares its own floor constant, as scheduleE /scheduleEZeroDollarFloor and form6251 /form8801PartsOneAndThreeZeroFloor do. Structural: it encodes the printed floor instruction, not a statutory dollar amount.

Fact.Name: The section 475(e)(2) trader's Schedule C net LOSS, deducted on Form 8960 line 10
Fact.Description: MOOT (resolves $0, Complete) on any return whose /scheduleCNetProfit is $0 or a profit, regardless of whether /writableSection475eTraderInFinancialInstrumentsOrCommoditiesElection is answered, because there is no loss for the special rule to deduct. On a return with a Schedule C net LOSS, this fact reads the attestation: unanswered resolves INCOMPLETE (disclosed) — whether the loss is deductible here depends on the attestation and there is no favorable default; answered false resolves $0 (an ordinary Schedule C loss is not this special rule's concern; it is captured elsewhere in the return, not on Form 8960 line 10); answered true resolves the loss's MAGNITUDE (a positive dollar amount, since line 10 is an additive deduction that reduces net investment income through line 11's subtraction, not a signed carry of the loss itself) — "you may use any net loss amount on your Schedule C ... as a deduction on line 10." A filer with more than one trade or business is NOT this population (i8960:1471 routes that case to a worksheet this dictionary does not model instead of the flat "any net loss amount" rule) — the attestation's own screen text tells such a filer to answer No and use /writableNiitLine10AdditionalModifications directly for any worksheet-allowed amount, so this fact does not attempt the worksheet. This is the SOLE-trading-business leg and it is mutually exclusive with the multi-business trader worksheets at /niitPrimaryFilerMultiBusinessTraderDeduction and /niitSecondaryFilerMultiBusinessTraderDeduction, which require this attestation to be answered FALSE; no return can take both.

Fact.Name: Form 8960 line 10, the Schedule 1 line 18 penalty on early withdrawal of savings
Fact.Description:
Form 8960 line 10 carries the Schedule 1 (Form 1040) line 18 penalty on early withdrawal of savings. The Instructions for Form 8960 state it as one closed-form sentence with no allocation, no election and no condition of allowance — "Early withdrawal penalty (Schedule 1 (Form 1040), line 18) is reported on Form 8960, line 10" — so the WHOLE of Schedule 1 line 18 is the line 10 amount. That figure is interest:/schedule1Line18EarlyWithdrawalPenalty, the total of Form 1099-INT box 2 across the return's interest reports, which IRC 62(a)(9) allows above the line rather than as an itemized deduction.
COMPLETE-SAFE AT ITS SOURCE, so this fact adds no guard of its own: /schedule1Line18EarlyWithdrawalPenalty puts its IsComplete arm first and resolves $0 on a return with no interest reports and on a return where box 2 is unanswered on every report. Every return with no early-withdrawal penalty is unchanged by this term.
POSITIVE, like every other line 10 term. Line 10 is an additive deduction that reduces net investment income through line 11's subtraction, so the penalty is entered as a positive magnitude and never as a negative modification.
THE CORRECTION IS ONE-SIDED, and the direction decides whom it reaches. The same penalty is an above-the-line deduction, so it has ALREADY reduced adjusted gross income and with it Form 8960 line 13 MAGI. On a return whose line 16 is the MAGI excess (line 15 smaller than line 12) this term moves lines 10, 11 and 12 and leaves line 17 exactly where it was — the tax was already right, because the deduction reached it through MAGI. On a return whose line 16 is net investment income, line 17 falls by 3.8 percent of the penalty: before this term such a filer paid the 3.8 percent on a deduction the instructions grant them.

Fact.Name: Form 8960 line 10, complete safe
Fact.Description:
The printed Form 8960 line 10 entry: /writableNiitLine10AdditionalModifications when answered, plus /niitSection475eTraderScheduleCNetLossModification, the section 475(e)(2) trader's Schedule C net loss automatically deducted once the trader attestation is answered true, plus /niitLine10EarlyWithdrawalPenalty, the Schedule 1 (Form 1040) line 18 penalty on early withdrawal of savings that the Line 7 instructions route to this line by a printed Note. Both derived terms are complete-safe, so a return that answers neither the trader attestation nor a Form 1099-INT box 2 resolves this line exactly as it did before either was added.
THE MULTI-BUSINESS TRADER WORKSHEET IS THE FOURTH AND FIFTH TERM, one per filer: /niitPrimaryFilerMultiBusinessTraderDeduction and /niitSecondaryFilerMultiBusinessTraderDeduction, each reading that filer's own Schedule SE line 3. They are mutually exclusive with the sole-trading-business leg above, which they require to be answered FALSE, and both are $0 until their own worksheet is opened.

Fact.Name: Form 8960 line 11, total deductions and modifications
Fact.Description: Form 8960 Part II line 11, "Total deductions and modifications. Add lines 9d and 10". Printed line 12 is "Net investment income. Subtract Part II, line 11, from Part I, line 8", and the superseded /netInvestmentIncome was the line 8 combine floored at $0 with no line 11 subtraction at all, because Part II was not modelled until that build. A return entering Part II amounts printed a line 11 its own line 12 ignored, which OVER stated net investment income and the tax on it. /netInvestmentIncome is now that subtraction, this fact is its subtrahend, and every addend here is complete safe so the rewire did not drop /netInvestmentIncome's completeness.

Fact.Name: Form 8960 line 15 before the zero floor, line 13 less line 14
Fact.Description: The signed subtraction behind Form 8960 Part III line 15, "Subtract line 14 from line 13": modified adjusted gross income (line 13, /niitMagi) less the filing status threshold (line 14, /niitThreshold). Negative on every return under the threshold, which is the common case, so the printed line 15 is this fact floored at $0. Helper only: the printed line is /niitLine15MagiOverTheThreshold.

Fact.Name: Form 8960 line 15, modified adjusted gross income over the threshold
Fact.Description: Form 8960 Part III line 15, "Subtract line 14 from line 13. If zero or less, enter -0-": the MAGI excess over the filing status threshold, floored at $0. This printed line deliberately has no completeness guard: its bare arithmetic preserves a Placeholder value and propagates genuine Incomplete when MAGI cannot be figured. Line 17 consumes this value through /niitLine16SmallerOfNetInvestmentIncomeOrMagiExcess, with the same status behavior.

Fact.Name: Form 8960 line 16, the smaller of line 12 and line 15
Fact.Description: Form 8960 Part III line 16, "Enter the smaller of line 12 or line 15": the base line 17 multiplies by 3.8 percent. Line 12 is /netInvestmentIncome, the fact the register already prints at f1_22, and line 15 is /niitLine15MagiOverTheThreshold. /niitLine17TaxWithResolvedMagi reads this fact so the printed line 16 and the tax it feeds are one computation and preserve Placeholder/Incompleteness alike. When the line 11 rewire obligation is met, line 12 changes for both at once because both read the same fact.

Fact.Name: Form 8960 line 1, taxable interest
Fact.Description: Form 8960 Part I line 1, "Taxable interest (see instructions)" = interest /interestIncome, the Form 1040 line 2b total. It is the SAME fact /netInvestmentIncome already adds as its line 1 term, so the printed line and the line 8 total cannot disagree. A direct alias rather than a complete safe one because /interestIncome is itself complete safe (line 8 adds it unguarded and stays Complete on every return), and an alias keeps the identity exact.

Fact.Name: Form 8960 line 2, ordinary dividends
Fact.Description: Form 8960 Part I line 2, "Ordinary dividends (see instructions)" = income /ordinaryDividends, the Form 1040 line 3b total. Qualified dividends are NOT added back: they are a subset of ordinary dividends, which is the reading /netInvestmentIncome records for the same term it already adds. Direct alias for the same reason as line 1.

Fact.Name: This 1099-R's box 2a taxable amount when box 7 carries distribution code D (Form 8960 line 3)
Fact.Description:
THIS Form 1099-R's box 2a taxable amount when its box 7 distribution code is D (nonqualified annuity or life insurance contract distribution) — "If code D is shown in box 7 of Form 1099-R, include on Form 8960, line 3, the taxable amount reported in box 2a." Code D can appear alone or paired with another code the same box carries (form1099RFrontier:/form1099Rs/*/isLawfulDistributionCodePair admits 1D, 2D, 3D, 4D, 7D and CD, and their reversed forms), so this fact tests form1099Rs:/form1099Rs/*/distributionCode against all thirteen bare-or-paired D forms, the same enumerated-Equal idiom form1099RFrontier:/form1099Rs/*/isRecognizedDistributionCode and /hasUnsupportedDistributionCode already use for this collection.
COMPLETE SAFE: form1099Rs:/form1099Rs/*/distributionCode is Incomplete when box 7 is unanswered (its own Switch carries no True fallback), so the code-match test is guarded by IsComplete on distributionCode itself and resolves $0 rather than Incomplete when box 7 was never entered; form1099Rs:/form1099Rs/*/taxableAmount is itself complete-safe ($0 when box 2a is unanswered). Summed by /niitLine3AnnuitiesFromCodeD.

Fact.Name: Total Form 1099-R box 2a taxable amount across every code-D distribution, for Form 8960 line 3
Fact.Description: CollectionSum(/form1099Rs/*/niitLine3CodeDAnnuityAmount) — the closed-form part of Form 8960 line 3 the Instructions state as a mechanical rule ("If code D is shown in box 7 of Form 1099-R, include on Form 8960, line 3, the taxable amount reported in box 2a"), added beside the filer's own /writableNiitLine3Annuities in /niitLine3Annuities. Complete safe: the CollectionSum sits inside an IsComplete Switch on the /form1099Rs collection defaulting to $0, and each item's term is itself complete-safe, so a return with no 1099-Rs (or none carrying code D) resolves Complete $0 and every committed scenario is byte-identical.

Fact.Name: Form 8960 line 3, annuities, complete safe
Fact.Description: The printed Form 8960 line 3 entry: /writableNiitLine3Annuities when the filer answered it, else $0, so every consumer of line 3 stays Complete on a return that never saw the question. This is the module's established intake shape, the /writableNiitLine5cPartnershipSCorpAdjustment and /niitLine5cPartnershipSCorpAdjustment pair. This line is now the line 3 term of /niitLine8TotalInvestmentIncome (Part I line 8, "Combine lines 1, 2, 3, 4c, 5d, 6, and 7"), which /netInvestmentIncome reads as the line 12 minuend. The superseded line 8 total added interest, dividends, line 5d, passive and royalty but not this term, so a return answering it printed a line 3 its own line 8 did not carry.

Fact.Name: Form 8960 line 4b, complete safe
Fact.Description: The printed Form 8960 line 4b entry: /writableNiitLine4bNonSection1411Adjustment when answered, else $0 — resolved for disclosure and record-keeping, exactly as printed. This fact does NOT reach /niitLine4cRentalRoyaltyAndPassthroughTotal. See /writableNiitLine4bNonSection1411Adjustment's own Description for why — this build's line-4a-equivalent components are already net of the nonpassive amount line 4b would otherwise back out, so wiring this adjustment into the total would double-subtract it. A filer's answer here is still Complete and printable, but affects no total.

Fact.Name: The section 475(e)(2) trader's Schedule C PROFIT, included in net investment income (Form 8960 line 4a/4c)
Fact.Description: SCHEDULE C ONLY: every source span that actually states the trader rule is Schedule-C-only (i8960:315, "deducted by a trader on Schedule C"; i8960:1469-1471, "your Schedule C ... net loss ... you don't need to complete Schedule SE"). i8960:31 is a generic statement about which schedules feed line 4a in general, not a trader-rule citation, and a farm is definitionally not a trading-in-financial-instruments-or-commodities business — no activityCode/businessCode/section475 field exists anywhere in scheduleC.xml or scheduleF.xml to distinguish a genuine trader's Schedule F from an ordinary farm, so a Schedule F profit is left to its ordinary NIIT treatment (excluded when materially participated, per section 1411(c)(6), unaffected by this fact) rather than folded into the trader special rule on no source authority. MOOT (resolves $0, Complete) on any return with no Schedule C profit — /scheduleCNetProfit at or below $0 — regardless of whether /writableSection475eTraderInFinancialInstrumentsOrCommoditiesElection is answered, because there is no profit for the attestation to gate. On a return with a Schedule C profit, this fact reads the attestation: unanswered resolves INCOMPLETE (disclosed), because whether the profit belongs in net investment income depends on the attestation and there is no favorable default to fall back on; answered false resolves $0 (an ordinary, materially-participating filer's Schedule C profit is excluded from NII by section 1411(c)(6), unaffected by this fact); answered true includes GreaterOf(/scheduleCNetProfit, $0) — profit only, because a LOSS is not this fact's concern (a Schedule C net loss is /niitSection475eTraderScheduleCNetLossModification's line-10 leg instead). The attestation itself IS the section 1402(a)(3) determination — a genuine section 475(e)(2) trader's activity is, by that election of facts, excepted from self-employment income, and income excepted from self-employment is included in NII once it otherwise meets the definition of NII (i8960:320-322, with the section 1402(a)(3)(A) capital-asset worked example at line 324). This fact does not gate on the dictionary's own /isSubjectToSelfEmploymentTax; that choice leaves a named gap.

Fact.Name: Form 8960 line 4c, rental, royalty and passthrough income combined with the 4b adjustment
Fact.Description: Form 8960 Part I line 4c, "Combine lines 4a and 4b". This dictionary models line 4a in three named pieces: /royaltyNetInvestmentIncome, the portfolio royalty component; /netPassiveIncomeForNiit, the section 469 passive component net of allowed losses; and /niitSection475eTraderScheduleCProfit, a section 475(e)(2) trader's own Schedule C PROFIT (see that fact's own Description for why Schedule F is excluded) — the SEVERAL-FACTS lead on this row names these three, which are addends of one printed line rather than candidates for it. NO 4b TERM: /niitLine4bNonSection1411Adjustment is not added here. See /writableNiitLine4bNonSection1411Adjustment's Description — this build's line-4a components are already net of the nonpassive portion the printed line 4b backs out, so a 4b term here would double-subtract it. REMAINING GAP, not built here: /royaltyNetInvestmentIncome and /netPassiveIncomeForNiit still do not cover an ORDINARY (non-trader) Schedule C or Schedule F business that is passive to the filer (not materially participated) — that amount is excluded from NII by section 1411(c)(6) because it is subject to self-employment tax on this dictionary's model (FED-8960-PASSIVE-469-001 defect 1's non-trader residue; a materially-participating filer's profit is correctly excluded either way, so this gap is only the passive/non-materially-participating case).

Fact.Name: Form 8960 line 6, the section 1296 mark-to-market PFIC adjustment leg, complete safe
Fact.Description: The derived /niitSection1296PositionsLine6Total when the section 1296 position collection is complete; otherwise /writableNiitLine6Section1296MarkToMarketAdjustment when answered, else $0. The collection-first arm binds the built annual mark computation to the first of the four line-6 sub-rules (i8960:715-741) without counting the legacy manual amount twice. The manual fallback remains for returns that have not supplied the position collection; the regular-income route for the same annual mark remains a separate successor. THE COLLECTION IS THE SELECTOR, not its resolved total. An ANSWERED position collection owns this leg outright - if a position in it is unresolved the leg stays Incomplete and the return refuses, where it previously fell through to the legacy manual box and on to $0 and silently understated line 6, line 8 and the tax. A legacy manual amount answered NONZERO beside an answered collection is a conflict and is also Incomplete, never a second amount and never an override; answered $0 beside the collection is not a conflict. An UNANSWERED collection is untouched: the legacy box, then $0, exactly as before.

Fact.Name: Form 8960 line 6, the section 1291 excess-distribution PFIC inclusion leg, complete safe
Fact.Description: /writableNiitLine6Section1291ExcessDistributionInclusion when answered, else $0 — the INTAKE SURFACE for the second of the four line-6 sub-rules (i8960:715-741), built this pass; the derivation from a PFIC's own section 1291 excess-distribution computation is not (no Form 8621, no PFIC surface anywhere in this dictionary — see /niitCfcPficLine6DerivedAdjustment in the records overlay).

Fact.Name: Form 8960 line 6, the CFC/QEF section 1.1411-10(g)-election-in-place inclusion leg, complete safe
Fact.Description: /writableNiitLine6CfcQefElectionInPlaceInclusion when the section 1.1411-10(g) election is in place and the amount is answered; STRUCTURALLY $0 when the election is answered false or left unanswered (mutually exclusive with /niitLine6CfcQefNoElectionAdjustment by the SAME header box, so an entered amount for the wrong regime never counts — review SHOULD FIX 1); Incomplete when the election IS in place and this amount is left unanswered, since i8960:729 states the inclusion as a required consequence of the checked box, never an optional one (review MUST FIX 1) — the INTAKE SURFACE for the third of the four line-6 sub-rules (i8960:715-741), built this pass; the derivation from a CFC/QEF's own section 951(a)/951A/1293(a) inclusion computation is not (no Form 5471, no CFC/QEF surface anywhere in this dictionary — see /niitCfcPficLine6DerivedAdjustment in the records overlay). THIS LEGACY LEG IS NOT READ when the per-holding /niitCfcQefHoldings collection is answered: line 6 then takes /niitCfcQefLine6Adjustment instead, and a nonzero amount in this legacy box makes that detail invalid so the return refuses rather than counting the same inclusion twice.

Fact.Name: Form 8960 line 6, the CFC/QEF no-section-1.1411-10(g)-election adjustment leg, complete safe
Fact.Description: /writableNiitLine6CfcQefNoElectionAdjustment when the section 1.1411-10(g) election is NOT in place and the amount is answered, else $0 (this leg's own source text is conditional -- "generally," a genuinely optional item, so no Incomplete arm is needed for its own unanswered amount); STRUCTURALLY $0, regardless of any answered amount, when the election IS in place (mutually exclusive with /niitLine6CfcQefElectionInPlaceInclusion by the SAME header box — review SHOULD FIX 1) — the INTAKE SURFACE for the fourth of the four line-6 sub-rules (i8960:715-741), built this pass; the derivation from a CFC/QEF's own previously-taxed-income distribution and basis-adjustment computation is not (no Form 5471, no CFC/QEF surface anywhere in this dictionary — see /niitCfcPficLine6DerivedAdjustment in the records overlay). THIS LEGACY LEG IS NOT READ when the per-holding /niitCfcQefHoldings collection is answered: line 6 then takes /niitCfcQefLine6Adjustment instead, and a nonzero amount in this legacy box makes that detail invalid so the return refuses rather than counting the same adjustment twice.

Fact.Name: Form 8960 line 6, complete safe
Fact.Description: The printed Form 8960 line 6 entry, now the sum of the four regime-specific intake legs the instructions itemize (i8960:715-741 — section 1296 mark-to-market, section 1291 excess distribution, the section 1.1411-10(g) election-in-place inclusion, and the no-election adjustment) plus /writableNiitLine6CfcAndPficAdjustments, which is RESCOPED by this addition to the residual: amounts NOT already itemized in the four legs above. Each of the five addends is independently complete safe, so a filer who answers only one leg (or none) does not need to also answer the others; do not enter the same CFC/PFIC dollar in more than one of the five boxes, or it is counted twice. LINE 8 combines lines 1, 2, 3, 4c, 5d, 6 and 7; /niitLine8TotalInvestmentIncome adds this line-6 term. The four regime writables are disclosed, filer-supplied amounts, not a derivation — this dictionary models no CFC, PFIC, QEF election, Form 5471 or Form 8621 anywhere, so the ACTUAL section 951(a)/951A/1293(a)/1291/1296 computations stay a named gap (Reg. section 1.1411-10 is unvendored — named per invariant #3, not cited); see /niitCfcPficLine6DerivedAdjustment in the records overlay for the narrowed derivation contract this build leaves open. THE TWO CFC/QEF AMOUNT LEGS ARE NOW AN EITHER/OR, NOT AN ALWAYS: when /niitCfcQefHoldings is answered line 6 reads /niitCfcQefLine6Adjustment, the per-holding reconciliation, and the two legacy amount legs are not read at all; when it is unanswered the two legacy legs are read exactly as before. A legacy amount answered nonzero beside an answered collection makes the detail invalid and line 6 Incomplete — it never falls back to the legacy pair, because that would count the same inclusion twice. The section 1296 and section 1291 legs and the residual writable are unchanged by that switch.

Fact.Name: This estate or trust K-1's box 14 code H amount for Form 8960 line 7 / MAGI
Fact.Description:
THIS Schedule K-1 (Form 1041)'s box 14 rows whose printed letter code is H — "Enter the amount from box 14, code H, of Schedule K-1 (Form 1041)" is the Form 8960 line 7 "Distributions from estates and trusts" rule verbatim. The box is recorded as a row list (scheduleE:/form1041K1s/*/otherInformationEntries) and every row of it is read, however many the K-1 lists; this fact sums a per-row part over the rows, the same shape scheduleE:/form1041K1s/*/estateTrustK1Box14GrossFarmingFishingIncome uses for code F: a row contributes its amount only when the row's code AND its amount are both answered and the code is H, and $0 otherwise, making the whole fact COMPLETE SAFE.
SIGNED, NOT FLOORED. The instruction states both signs explicitly: "If the amount ... is a positive number, enter it on Form 8960, line 7 ... If the amount ... is a negative number ... enter it on Form 8960, line 7." The row amounts (scheduleE:/form1041K1s/*/otherInformationEntries/*/writableAmount) carry no Min limit, so the recorded amount is whatever the K-1 prints, sign included, and this fact passes it through unchanged.
Declared here rather than in scheduleE.xml because only Form 8960 line 7 / line 13 read code H (scheduleE's own box-14 routing table has no line for it) — the same cross-module collection-extension estimatedPayments.xml uses for box 13 code A (/form1041K1s/*/estateTrustK1Box13CreditForEstimatedTaxes). Summed by /niitEstateTrustK1Box14CodeHTotal.

Fact.Name: This estate or trust K-1's box 14 code H amount for Form 8960 line 7 / MAGI: this row's part
Fact.Description: One row of /form1041K1s/*/otherInformationEntries as /form1041K1s/*/niitBox14CodeHAmount reads it: this row's amount when the row's code is H, both the code and the amount are answered; otherwise $0. Complete on every row, because the code and amount tests open on IsComplete, so the reader over the row table is Complete once the table is answered.

Fact.Name: Total Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) box 14 code H across every attached K-1, for Form 8960 line 7
Fact.Description: CollectionSum(/form1041K1s/*/niitBox14CodeHAmount), the Form 8960 line 7 "Enter the amount from box 14, code H" rule aggregated over every estate/trust K-1 the return carries — the estates-and-trusts leg of line 7, added beside the existing writable and the Form 8814 line 12 leg in /niitLine7OtherModifications. SIGNED, matching the per-item fact. Complete-safe: the CollectionSum sits inside an IsComplete Switch on the /form1041K1s collection defaulting to $0, and each item's term is itself complete-safe, so a return that never opened the estate or trust K-1 section resolves Complete $0 and every committed scenario is byte-identical (none answers box 14 code H).

Fact.Name: MAGI Worksheet line 3 adjustment for a positive box 14 code H amount
Fact.Description: The Form 8960 line 13 MAGI Worksheet line 3 term for a positive box 14 code H amount: GreaterOf(/niitEstateTrustK1Box14CodeHTotal, $0). The instruction's Note states two different rules by sign — "If the amount reported ... is a positive number, enter it on Form 8960, line 7, and increase your MAGI on Form 8960, line 13 ... by the same amount" is UNCONDITIONAL, while a NEGATIVE amount's MAGI effect applies only "as necessary" when "the trust has indicated some (or all) of the adjustment also requires a MAGI adjustment" — a fact this dictionary has no source for (the trust's own indication is not on the K-1's printed boxes). Flooring at $0 applies the unconditional positive rule and withholds the conditional negative one until that indication is modelled, which is the SAME floored-subtraction discipline /niitMagiForeignEarnedIncomeAddback already uses for its own conservative reading. A negative code H amount therefore still reduces line 7 / NII (see /niitEstateTrustK1Box14CodeHTotal, unfloored) but does not reduce MAGI here. Complete-safe by construction (GreaterOf of a complete-safe total).

Fact.Name: Form 8960 line 7, complete safe
Fact.Description:
The printed Form 8960 line 7 entry: /writableNiitLine7OtherModifications when answered, else $0. Line 8 combines lines 1, 2, 3, 4c, 5d, 6 and 7 and the superseded total carried no line 7 term at all; /niitLine8TotalInvestmentIncome now adds this one. PLUS FORM 8814 LINE 12, the one line 7 modification this dictionary can COMPUTE. The Instructions for Form 8960, Line 7, name it by number: "Parents electing to include their child's dividends and capital gain distributions in their income by filing Form 8814 must include on Form 8960, line 7, the amount on Form 8814, line 12, excluding Alaska Permanent Fund Dividends", so form8814:/form8814TotalLine12OtherIncome (the child's ordinary inclusion, summed over the attached Forms 8814) is added beside the hand-entered writable. The writable stays for every OTHER line 7 item the instructions list (the ones the graph does not compute), and the intake prompt for it must now say "do not include Form 8814 line 12 — it is added for you", or a filer who copies their own line 12 into it counts it twice; that prompt edit is an application item. The child's line 9 qualified dividends and line 10 capital gain distributions are NOT here: they reach line 2 through income:/ordinaryDividends and line 5d through the capital-gain chain, and the instruction names line 12 only. [UPDATED: THE ALASKA PERMANENT FUND EXCLUSION IS NOW APPLIED. The instruction's own clause is "excluding Alaska Permanent Fund Dividends", and this addend is form8814:/form8814TotalLine12OtherIncomeExcludingAlaskaPermanentFundDividends — the module total of each child's line 12 less the Permanent Fund part of it, figured by the ONE printed method for this exclusion, Publication 550's "start with the amount on Form 8814, line 6. Multiply that amount by a percentage that is equal to the Alaska Permanent Fund dividends divided by the total amount on Form 8814, line 4. Subtract the result from the amount on Form 8814, line 12." Publication 550 writes that method for the Form 4952 investment-income test rather than for this line, so carrying it here is an analogy and is marked provisional on the facts that make it. An Alaska family's NIIT is no longer over-stated by 3.8% of the child's Permanent Fund share.] Complete-safe $0 on every return with no election, and equal to the whole of line 12 whenever no Permanent Fund amount is answered, so every committed scenario is byte-identical. The same Line 7 instruction lists "Casualty and theft losses reported on Schedule A (Form 1040), Itemized Deductions, line 15 (enter as a negative amount)" among the gains and losses from dispositions not included on line 5a, and form4684:/casualtyLossDeduction (Form 4684 line 18) is exactly that number. It is gated on scheduleA:/claimsItemizedDeductions, because a standard-deduction filer deducted nothing on Schedule A line 15. Complete-safe $0 on every return with no Form 4684 event, so every committed scenario is byte-identical. A net qualified disaster loss is NOT here: that reaches Schedule A line 16 and the standard deduction, a different printed line from the one the instruction names.]
THE SECTION 1411 NOL DEDUCTION IS THE SIXTH TERM: /niitNolLine7Modification, the negative of the applicable portion of each loss year's regular NOL used on this return. $0 when the loss-component collection is unanswered.

Fact.Name: Form 8960 line 7, the Schedule A line 15 casualty and theft loss, as a negative modification
Fact.Description:
The Instructions for Form 8960 name this item on line 7 by its printed Schedule A line and by its sign: among the "Gains and losses from the disposition of property not included on line 5a that are taken into account in computing taxable income" the instructions list "Casualty and theft losses reported on Schedule A (Form 1040), Itemized Deductions, line 15 (enter as a negative amount)." So this fact is form4684:/casualtyLossDeduction — Form 4684 line 18, the personal casualty and theft loss deduction that Schedule A line 15 carries — SUBTRACTED FROM ZERO, because the printed entry is negative and line 7 is a signed addend of line 8.
GATED ON ITEMIZING, and the gate is the printed line rather than a policy choice. The instruction names Schedule A line 15, and a filer taking the standard deduction deducted nothing on Schedule A line 15 at all; section 1411(c)(1)(B) reaches only deductions "allowed by this subtitle", so there is nothing for line 7 to mirror. The gate is scheduleA:/claimsItemizedDeductions, the same gate /niitLine9aInvestmentInterestDeductedOnScheduleA uses for the Schedule A line 9 investment interest.
THE POPULATION IS FORM 4684 SECTION A, PERSONAL-USE PROPERTY, AND ONLY THAT. form4684:/casualtyLossDeduction is Form 4684 line 18 = line 16 less line 17, gated by form4684:/claimsCasualtyLoss and floored at zero. FORM 4684 SECTION B HAS TWO DOORS AND ONLY ONE OF THEM IS FORM 4797: column (b)(i), trade-or-business property, leaves through Form 4797 line 14 (Form 4684 lines 31 and 38a), which is Form 8960 line 5a's territory rather than this line's; column (b)(ii), INCOME-PRODUCING property, leaves on Form 4684 lines 32 and 38b to SCHEDULE A LINE 16, as form4684:/incomeProducingCasualtyLoss, an addend of scheduleA:/otherItemizedDeductions. Neither Section B column is this fact.
A SECOND LINE-7 RESIDUE, NAMED NOT CARRIED, and it follows from that second door. The Line 7 bullet this fact implements introduces its two sub-items with "for example", so the list is illustrative rather than closed: a casualty or theft loss of INCOME-PRODUCING property, deducted on Schedule A line 16, is a loss from a disposition of property not included on line 5a and taken into account in computing taxable income, and is therefore a candidate negative line-7 modification the instructions do not name by number. This fact does NOT carry it — the instruction names Schedule A line 15 and nothing else — and a filer with such a loss can still enter it in the line-7 residual box. Naming it is the point: it is a residue of the printed list's own openness, not a gap in the sentence the instruction does state. Section 165(h)(5)(A) confines a personal casualty loss in this tax year to one "attributable to a Federally declared disaster" except to the extent of personal casualty gains, so on most returns line 18 is already zero for a non-disaster loss and this term with it.
WHAT IS NOT CARRIED, stated because it is a different printed line and not an oversight: a NET QUALIFIED DISASTER LOSS (form4684:/netQualifiedDisasterLoss, Form 4684 line 15) reaches Schedule A LINE 16 and increases the standard deduction instead, and the instruction for this line names Schedule A line 15 only. This fact does not carry it, and a qualified-disaster filer's Form 8960 line 7 is unaffected by that loss.
COMPLETE-SAFE BY CONSTRUCTION, and the fallback is unreachable on any filable return. form4684:/casualtyLossDeduction resolves Complete $0 on every return that reports no casualty or theft event, but it CAN resolve Incomplete on a return that reports an event with an unanswered input — so this fact reads it under an IsComplete guard and resolves $0 rather than dragging Form 8960 line 8, net investment income and the Schedule 2 attachment gate into an Incomplete they cannot describe. That $0 cannot be the answer on a return anyone can file: an itemizing filer whose Form 4684 line 18 is Incomplete also has an Incomplete Schedule A line 15, hence Incomplete total itemized deductions and Incomplete taxable income, so the return does not resolve at all. The moment the Form 4684 inputs are answered the deduction appears here.

Fact.Name: Working-capital investment income, one record per business
Fact.Description: One record per trade or business whose WORKING CAPITAL earned interest or dividends that the filer reported inside a Schedule C or Schedule F line rather than on Schedule B. This per-business route replaces the single return-level box /writableNiitWorkingCapitalInterestAndDividendsInBusinessIncome, not any other Form 8960 line 7 modification; when it is unanswered that box and its existing section 475(e)(2) trader rule are read exactly as before. An explicitly empty collection means there are no such businesses and adds zero; an unanswered collection leaves the legacy route in charge. A legacy amount answered nonzero beside an answered collection makes the line Incomplete rather than falling back, because the same interest would otherwise be counted twice. This route models interest and dividends only. A capital gain or loss on working capital that is not reported on line 5a goes in the line 7 other-modifications box (/writableNiitLine7OtherModifications), as the instructions direct for a disposition gain or loss not reported there; deductions properly allocable to working-capital income go in the line 10 box (/writableNiitLine10AdditionalModifications). No automatic Schedule C, Schedule F or Schedule K-1 source join exists: the filer opens a record.

Fact.Name: This record is the return on capital the business is holding, not ordinary-course receivable interest
Fact.Description: SCREEN. Question: "Is this interest or these dividends earned on money the business was HOLDING, such as its cash reserves, bank deposits, certificates of deposit or short-term investments?" Help text: section 469(e)(1)(B), applied to the net investment income tax by section 1411(c)(3), reaches only income attributable to an INVESTMENT of working capital. Interest on the business's OWN notes and accounts receivable, arising from its own sales or taken in payment for them, is ordinary-course income of that trade or business and is NOT this amount; answer false for such a record. Asked when: a working-capital record is opened. Unanswered posture: the record does not resolve and the line-7 modification is Incomplete; a blank is never read as false, because a false answer zeroes a positive modification and that is the taxpayer-favourable direction. Validation: Boolean, required on an opened record. What the answer feeds: this record's line-7 contribution.

Fact.Name: These amounts are inside the business income already on the return
Fact.Description: SCREEN. Question: "Are these amounts already inside the Schedule C or Schedule F figures on your return, rather than on Schedule B?" Help text: Schedule C line 6, "Interest (such as on notes and accounts receivable)", is where such an amount is reported; Schedule F's other-income line does the same job. Form 8960 lines 1 and 2 already carry whatever is on Form 1040 line 2b and line 3b whole, so an amount reported there must NOT be entered here or it is counted twice. Asked when: a working-capital record is opened. Unanswered posture: the record does not resolve and the line-7 modification is Incomplete. KNOWN GAP, stated rather than defaulted: an explicit FALSE also leaves this record Incomplete in this build. The amount is then already on line 1 or line 2 and the correct line-7 contribution is zero, but no arm computes that yet; a filer in that position must leave the record out of the collection. Validation: Boolean, required on an opened record. What the answer feeds: this record's line-7 contribution.

Fact.Name: Interest earned on this business's working capital
Fact.Description: SCREEN. Question: "How much INTEREST did this business earn on the money it was holding?" Help text: enter only amounts that are inside this business's Schedule C or Schedule F figures. Asked when: a working-capital record is opened. Unanswered posture: the record does not resolve and the line-7 modification is Incomplete; an unanswered live amount is not zero, so enter zero explicitly if there is none. Validation: Dollar, Min $0. A NEGATIVE answer is refused by the record's own arithmetic rather than by the limit, because the limit is an intake validation and is not enforced on resolution. What the answer feeds: this record's line-7 contribution, and through it Form 8960 line 7, line 8 and line 12.

Fact.Name: Dividends earned on this business's working capital
Fact.Description: SCREEN. Question: "How much in DIVIDENDS did this business earn on the money it was holding?" Help text: enter only amounts that are inside this business's Schedule C or Schedule F figures. Asked when: a working-capital record is opened. Unanswered posture: the record does not resolve and the line-7 modification is Incomplete; an unanswered live amount is not zero, so enter zero explicitly if there is none. Validation: Dollar, Min $0. A NEGATIVE answer is refused by the record's own arithmetic rather than by the limit, because the limit is an intake validation and is not enforced on resolution. What the answer feeds: this record's line-7 contribution, and through it Form 8960 line 7, line 8 and line 12.

Fact.Name: The part of this record's interest and dividends already somewhere else on Form 8960
Fact.Description: SCREEN. Question: "How much of that interest and those dividends is ALREADY counted somewhere else on Form 8960?" Help text: this subtraction is what keeps the same dollar from being counted twice. The commonest case is a business whose whole profit already reaches Form 8960 line 4a, including a section 475(e)(2) trading business: the interest inside that profit is already in net investment income and belongs here in full. Asked when: a working-capital record is opened. Unanswered posture: the record does not resolve and the line-7 modification is Incomplete; a blank is never read as zero, because zero is the subtraction-free and taxpayer-adverse answer and it must be stated, not assumed. Validation: Dollar, Min $0, and it may not exceed this record's interest plus dividends. Both bounds are re-tested on resolution and a record that breaks either one stays Incomplete rather than producing a number. What the answer feeds: this record's line-7 contribution.

Fact.Name: This business's working-capital interest and dividends not already in net investment income
Fact.Description: Interest plus dividends less the part already counted elsewhere on Form 8960. A record whose income is NOT the return on held capital contributes $0. Every other record must answer all five of its questions, all three amounts must be nonnegative, and the already-counted part may not exceed the interest and dividends it is subtracted from; a record that fails any of those stays Incomplete rather than producing a number, because each failure mode would otherwise move net investment income in an unverified direction. The Min $0 limits on the three amount intakes are intake validation and are NOT enforced when the graph resolves, so the nonnegativity tests are repeated here. Capital gains and losses on working capital, and deductions allocable to this income, are not computed by this record.

Fact.Name: Total per-business working-capital addition to Form 8960 line 7
Fact.Description: Zero if the per-business detail collection is unopened, so no return that has never seen this route moves. When the collection is answered, the sum of its records' contributions; an answered but unresolved record leaves the total Incomplete and it never silently falls back to the legacy return-level box. An explicitly empty collection sums to zero. This total is per business and is not zeroed by the return-level section 475(e)(2) trader attestation, which is an attestation about ONE trading business and says nothing about another business's cash reserves; a trading business whose interest is already inside Form 8960 line 4a subtracts that interest on its own record instead.

Fact.Name: Form 8960 line 7, working-capital interest and dividends the filer reported inside business income
Fact.Description:
A positive Form 8960 line 7 modification for interest and dividends earned on a trade or business's WORKING CAPITAL that the filer reported inside a Schedule C or Schedule F line rather than on Schedule B — and which therefore reach neither line 1 nor line 2. The Instructions for Form 8960 give line 7 exactly this job: "Other items of NII (or properly allocable deductions) not otherwise included on Form 8960".
WHY IT IS IN NET INVESTMENT INCOME AT ALL, and this is a statute-only rule the Form 8960 instructions never state: section 1411(c)(3) applies "a rule similar to the rule of section 469(e)(1)(B)", under which "any income, gain, or loss which is attributable to an investment of working capital shall be treated as not derived in the ordinary course of a trade or business." So the return on money a business holds rather than deploys is investment income however the business itself is characterized under section 469 — including for a business whose ordinary profit reaches Form 8960 by no path at all.
THE POPULATION IS NARROW AND IT IS STATED, because the fence is the whole design. It is ONLY amounts a Schedule C or Schedule F line already carries — Schedule C line 6, "Interest (such as on notes and accounts receivable)", is where such an amount is reported. TWO EXCLUSIONS, and the first is the statute's own boundary. (1) INTEREST ON THE BUSINESS'S OWN NOTES AND ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE IS NOT THIS AMOUNT. Section 469(e)(1)(B) reaches income "attributable to an investment of working capital", and a receivable arising from the business's own sales, or a note taken in payment for them, is ordinary-course income of that trade or business rather than the return on capital the business is holding. Only the second kind belongs here: interest or dividends on cash reserves, bank deposits, certificates of deposit and short-term investments the business holds. (2) It is NOT interest or dividends already on Form 1040 line 2b or line 3b — Form 8960 lines 1 and 2 carry those whole and entering them again would count them twice.
STRUCTURALLY $0 FOR A SECTION 475(e)(2) TRADER, and the moot arm comes first for the same reason it does on the trader's own line-10 fact. When /writableSection475eTraderInFinancialInstrumentsOrCommoditiesElection is answered TRUE the trading business's whole Schedule C profit is already in Form 8960 line 4a through /niitSection475eTraderScheduleCProfit, with any interest inside it, and on a loss return the interest is already netted into the line-10 magnitude; a second entry here would double-count it. An UNANSWERED attestation does not make this line Incomplete: the amount the filer entered is included, which is the taxpayer-adverse direction and never a favourable default.
Complete-safe on every arm, so no committed return moves and the Schedule 2 attachment gate is untouched.
A PER-BUSINESS ROUTE IN FRONT OF THE RETURN-LEVEL BOX. When /niitWorkingCapitalItems is ANSWERED it owns this line: the total is /niitWorkingCapitalLine7DerivedAdjustment and the return-level box is not read at all. An unresolved record leaves the line Incomplete rather than falling back, because a fallback would drop a stated amount. A return-level box answered NONZERO beside an answered collection is a conflict and is also Incomplete; answered $0 beside it is not. THE PER-BUSINESS ROUTE DOES NOT READ THE SECTION 475(e)(2) TRADER ATTESTATION, and that is deliberate: the attestation is one return-level answer about ONE trading business and says nothing about a DIFFERENT business's cash reserves, so zeroing every business off it would delete real net investment income. The double-count it was there to prevent is handled per record instead, by /niitWorkingCapitalItems/*/writableAlreadyIncludedInNiit, which the trading business subtracts its own already-on-line-4a interest on. The direction of that trade is stated: a filer who opens a record for the trading business and leaves that subtraction at $0 is OVER-taxed, where the old return-level moot could only UNDER-tax. An UNANSWERED collection is untouched: the trader moot, then the return-level box, then $0, exactly as before, and this Description's paragraphs above still describe that path in full.

Fact.Name: Form 8960 line 9a before the completeness guard, the Schedule A line 9 investment interest
Fact.Description: The individual filer's Form 8960 line 9a figure. The instructions are specific about which number it is: "Enter on Form 8960, line 9a, interest expense you paid or accrued during the tax year deducted on Schedule A (Form 1040), line 9", and Schedule A line 9 is form4952 /investmentInterestExpenseDeduction, the Form 4952 line 8 deduction that dictionary/pdf/2025/IRS1040SA maps to that printed line. It is therefore gated on scheduleA /claimsItemizedDeductions: a filer taking the standard deduction deducted nothing on Schedule A line 9, so their line 9a is $0 even where Form 4952 would allow a deduction. The estates and trusts sentence in the same instruction (enter the amount from Form 4952 line 8) is not this arm, and the Form 1040-NR residency scoping is out of this dictionary's return type. Helper only: the printed line is /niitLine9aInvestmentInterestExpenses.

Fact.Name: Form 8960 line 9a, investment interest expenses
Fact.Description: The printed Form 8960 Part II line 9a entry: /niitLine9aInvestmentInterestDeductedOnScheduleA when it resolves, else $0. The guard is what keeps line 9d and line 11 Complete on a partial return: the switch reads scheduleA /claimsItemizedDeductions, which is unresolved on a scenario that never reached the deduction question, while the line 9b and 9c intakes beside it are complete safe by construction. One caveat the instructions state and this build does not model: investment interest already taken into account on line 4a through Schedule E must not be entered again here.

Fact.Name: Form 8960 line 9b, complete safe
Fact.Description: The printed Form 8960 line 9b entry: /writableNiitLine9bStateLocalAndForeignIncomeTax when answered, else $0, so line 9d and line 11 stay Complete on a return that entered no Part II amount.

Fact.Name: Form 8960 line 9c, complete safe
Fact.Description: The printed Form 8960 line 9c entry: /writableNiitLine9cMiscellaneousInvestmentExpenses when answered, else $0.

Fact.Name: Form 8960 line 9d, total investment expenses
Fact.Description: Form 8960 Part II line 9d, "Add lines 9a, 9b, and 9c": the sum of the three complete safe Part II expense facts. Complete on every return because each addend is, so line 11 and any future line 12 subtraction inherit that.

Fact.Name: Form 8960 Part I header, the Regulations section 1.1411-10(g) election box
Fact.Description: Form 8960 Part I header box three, "Regulations section 1.1411-10(g) election (see instructions)": the election to treat inclusions from a controlled foreign corporation or a qualified electing fund as net investment income in the year they are included for regular tax. This dictionary models no CFC, PFIC or QEF interest at all (the module header records line 6 as deferred for that reason, and /niitMagi treats the MAGI worksheet CFC and PFIC line as structurally zero), so nothing can derive the election and it is an intake. Printed as the record field it is.

Fact.Name: Form 8960 line 10, additional modifications (writable)
Fact.Description: Form 8960 Part II line 10, "Additional modifications (see instructions)": the deductions and modifications properly allocable to net investment income that lines 1 through 9 do not already reflect. Do NOT enter a section 475(e)(2) trader's own Schedule C net loss here when trading in financial instruments or commodities is the filer's only business — that amount is added for you (/niitSection475eTraderScheduleCNetLossModification) once /writableSection475eTraderInFinancialInstrumentsOrCommoditiesElection is answered; entering it again here counts it twice. A filer with more than one trade or business is NOT covered by that automatic amount (the printed instructions route that case to a worksheet this dictionary does not model) and answers this box directly for any trading-business Schedule C amount the worksheet would allow. Do NOT enter the Schedule 1 (Form 1040) line 18 penalty on early withdrawal of savings here either — the instructions' own Note reports that penalty on this line and it is added for you (/niitLine10EarlyWithdrawalPenalty) from the Form 1099-INT box 2 amounts already recorded; entering it again here counts it twice. Do not enter a multi-business trading expense here either: the per-filer worksheets at /writableNiitPrimaryFilerTradingExpensesNotOtherwiseDeducted and /writableNiitSecondaryFilerTradingExpensesNotOtherwiseDeducted carry it to line 10.

Fact.Name: Return-level attestation: the filer's only trade or business is trading in financial instruments or commodities (section 475(e)(2))
Fact.Description: SCREEN. Question: "Is trading in financial instruments or commodities your ONLY trade or business?" Help text: answer Yes only if trading in financial instruments or commodities — as defined in section 475(e)(2) — is the ONE trade or business the filer operates; a filer who also runs any other trade or business (a second Schedule C, a farm that is not itself a trading business, and so on) does not qualify and should answer No, because the printed instructions route a filer with more than one trade or business to a worksheet this dictionary does not model (the filer enters any trading-business Schedule C amount the worksheet allows directly on the line 10 box instead). A qualifying trader does not complete Schedule SE for that business and may deduct any Schedule C net loss as a Form 8960 line 10 modification instead of the ordinary self-employment exclusion; a qualifying trader's Schedule C or Schedule F PROFIT is net investment income, because it is excepted from self-employment income and income excepted from self-employment is included in NII when it otherwise meets the definition of NII. Asked when: the return reports a Schedule C or Schedule F net profit or a Schedule C net loss. Unanswered posture: a return with no Schedule C or Schedule F profit or loss is unaffected (moot) regardless of the answer; a return with an unanswered attestation AND a Schedule C or Schedule F profit, or a Schedule C loss, resolves the line this fact feeds to Incomplete (disclosed) rather than silently defaulting to "not a trader" — the attestation is a condition of the profit's inclusion in net investment income and of the loss's line-10 deduction, not a favorable default either return-level fact should ever assume. Validation: Boolean. What the answer feeds: a Yes answer includes any Schedule C or Schedule F PROFIT in net investment income (Form 8960 line 4a/4c) and any Schedule C NET LOSS as a Form 8960 line 10 additional modification; a No answer, or a return this fact is moot on, leaves both lines unaffected. ANSWER THIS FALSE, NOT BLANK, for a filer who trades in financial instruments or commodities AND carries another trade or business: that filer uses the per-filer multi-business trader worksheet instead, and the worksheet requires this attestation to be an explicit FALSE.

Fact.Name: Form 8960 line 3, annuities from nonqualified plans (writable)
Fact.Description: SCREEN. Question: "How much did you receive in 2025 from annuities you hold as investments?" Help text: enter the TAXABLE part of distributions from NONQUALIFIED annuities and commercial annuity contracts — the amount already on Form 1040 line 5b for that contract. Distributions from qualified plans and IRAs under sections 401(a), 403(a), 403(b), 408, 408A and 457(b) are excluded and are NOT this line. Do not enter interest, ordinary dividends or royalties here: those reach both forms on their own from the documents already recorded, so entering them here counts them twice. Do NOT enter a 1099-R distribution coded D in box 7 either — that taxable amount is added for you (/niitLine3AnnuitiesFromCodeD), which is the one case the graph CAN separate a nonqualified commercial annuity from a qualified plan distribution: code D is the printed discriminator. This box remains for every OTHER source of annuity income the graph cannot identify from a document already on file (for example a nonqualified annuity paid outside the 1099-R universe this dictionary models). Asked when: the return is completing Form 8960, OR form4952:/form4952Line1Answered is true — TWO FORMS, ONE QUESTION. Section 1411(c)(1)(A)(i) puts the amount on Form 8960 line 3; section 163(d)(5)(A)(i), through section 469(e)(1)(A)(i)(I), puts the same dollar on Form 4952 line 4a, and a Form 4952 filer below the section 1411 threshold must still be asked. Unanswered posture: DEFAULTED to $0 through /niitLine3Annuities — taxpayer-favourable on Form 8960 (a lower line 3 is a lower NIIT base) and taxpayer-ADVERSE on Form 4952 (a lower line 4a is a lower line 6 ceiling, so line 8 is too small and line 7 too large), so the screen should be shown rather than skipped. Validation: Dollar, Min $0, no Max; ONE return-level amount, not one per contract. What the answer feeds: Form 8960 line 3 → line 8 → line 12; and Form 4952 line 4a → line 6 → line 8 → Schedule A line 9 → /totalItemizedDeductions, and Form 4952 line 7.

Fact.Name: Form 8960 line 4b, the non section 1411 trade or business adjustment (writable)
Fact.Description: Form 8960 Part I line 4b, "Adjustment for net income or loss derived in the ordinary course of a non-section 1411 trade or business." THE PRINTED MECHANISM IS GROSS-THEN-SUBTRACT: line 4a carries the taxpayer's WHOLE Schedule C/E/F total, and line 4b is where the filer backs OUT the nonpassive (materially-participated) portion as a negative adjustment. THIS BUILD DOES NOT WORK THAT WAY: its line-4a-equivalent components — /netPassiveIncomeForNiit and /royaltyNetInvestmentIncome — are each ALREADY NET of the nonpassive portion at the source (see their own Descriptions), so there is nothing left on this build's line 4c for a 4b adjustment to back out. Entering the amount the printed instructions ask for here would DOUBLE-subtract nonpassive income that this build never added in the first place. Because of that, /niitLine4cRentalRoyaltyAndPassthroughTotal no longer reads this fact (see that fact's Description for the wiring history). This box remains a printed, disclosed, filer-supplied field — the return still needs to be able to record what the filer wrote here — but no total in this build consumes it. A future unit that models line 4a as the true printed gross (Schedule C/F included unfiltered, per FED-8960-PASSIVE-469-001 defect 1) would need to re-derive this box's semantics from scratch, not resume this one. SEQUENCING CONSTRAINT for that build: whatever backs the nonpassive portion out of a printed-gross line 4a must carve the WORKING-CAPITAL slice out of the back-out, because section 1411(c)(3) keeps interest and dividends on a business's working capital inside net investment income however the business is characterized under section 469.

Fact.Name: Form 8960 line 6, other adjustments for certain CFCs and PFICs not itemized in the four regime-specific boxes (writable)
Fact.Description: SCREEN. Question: "Do you have any OTHER Form 8960 line 6 CFC/PFIC adjustment not already entered above?" Help text: Form 8960 Part I line 6, "Adjustments to investment income for certain CFCs and PFICs," covers four regimes the instructions itemize separately — section 1296 mark-to-market, section 1291 excess distribution, the section 1.1411-10(g) election-in-place inclusion, and the no-election adjustment (each now its own box: /writableNiitLine6Section1296MarkToMarketAdjustment, /writableNiitLine6Section1291ExcessDistributionInclusion, /writableNiitLine6CfcQefElectionInPlaceInclusion, /writableNiitLine6CfcQefNoElectionAdjustment). THIS BOX IS THE RESIDUAL — any line-6 amount not already itemized in one of those four. Entering an amount here that is also entered in one of the four regime boxes counts it twice. This dictionary models no CFC, PFIC or QEF interest anywhere, which is why /niitMagi treats the corresponding MAGI worksheet line as structurally zero, so every line-6 box (this one and the four regime boxes) is an intake rather than a derivation. Asked when: the filer owns stock, directly or indirectly, in a CFC or PFIC. Unanswered posture: DEFAULTED to $0 through /niitLine6CfcAndPficAdjustments — disclosed, filer-supplied, not a claimed benefit gated by a condition of allowance. Validation: Dollar, no Min/Max (signed, since the underlying regimes can each increase or decrease NII). What the answer feeds: Form 8960 line 6 → line 8 → line 12.

Fact.Name: Form 8960 line 6, the section 1296 mark-to-market PFIC adjustment (writable)
Fact.Description: SCREEN. Question: "How much do you need to add to or subtract from your net investment income under the section 1296 mark-to-market PFIC rules?" Help text: if you are subject to the section 1296 mark-to-market rules for a passive foreign investment company (PFIC), include in net investment income any amount included in income for regular income tax purposes under section 1296(a)(1), and deduct from net investment income any amount deducted from income for regular income tax purposes under section 1296(a)(2) — but only for items not otherwise already reflected on Form 8960 (do not enter an amount already counted on another Form 8960 line). Enter a positive number for a net increase, a negative number for a net decrease. Asked when: the filer owns stock, directly or indirectly, in a PFIC subject to the section 1296 mark-to-market election. Unanswered posture: DEFAULTED to $0 through /niitLine6Section1296MarkToMarketAdjustment — disclosed. Validation: Dollar, no Min/Max (signed — the source states both an inclusion and a deduction arm). What the answer feeds: Form 8960 line 6 → line 8 → line 12.

Fact.Name: Form 8960 line 6, the section 1291 excess-distribution PFIC inclusion (writable)
Fact.Description: SCREEN. Question: "How much did you include in net investment income under the section 1291 excess-distribution PFIC rules?" Help text: if you are subject to the section 1291 rules for a PFIC, include in net investment income any excess distributions that are dividends for NIIT purposes, as well as any gains treated as excess distributions for regular income tax purposes — but only for items not otherwise already reflected on Form 8960. Asked when: the filer owns stock, directly or indirectly, in a PFIC subject to the section 1291 excess-distribution rules. Unanswered posture: DEFAULTED to $0 through /niitLine6Section1291ExcessDistributionInclusion — disclosed. Validation: Dollar, Min $0 (the source states only an inclusion, no deduction arm). What the answer feeds: Form 8960 line 6 → line 8 → line 12.

Fact.Name: Form 8960 line 6, the CFC/QEF section 1.1411-10(g)-election-in-place inclusion (writable)
Fact.Description: SCREEN. Question: "How much did you include in net investment income because of your section 1.1411-10(g) election for a CFC or QEF?" Help text: if you have a Regulations section 1.1411-10(g) election in effect for a controlled foreign corporation (CFC) or qualified electing fund (QEF), include in net investment income any inclusion under section 951(a), 951A or 1293(a) derived from the CFC or QEF — but not an inclusion under section 1293(a)(1)(B), which may already be reported elsewhere on Form 8960 (such as line 5a), and not an amount otherwise already reflected on Form 8960. Asked when: /writableNiitCfcAndQefRegulationElection is answered true (the Form 8960 Part I header box for this same election). Unanswered posture: DEFAULTED to $0 through /niitLine6CfcQefElectionInPlaceInclusion — disclosed. Validation: Dollar, Min $0 (the source states only an inclusion for this regime). What the answer feeds: Form 8960 line 6 → line 8 → line 12. LEAVE THIS BLANK OR ZERO whenever the per-holding /niitCfcQefHoldings collection is answered. The two boxes describe the same inclusions, so an amount in both is a contradiction and makes line 6 Incomplete rather than counting the inclusion twice.

Fact.Name: Form 8960 line 6, the CFC/QEF no-section-1.1411-10(g)-election adjustment (writable)
Fact.Description: SCREEN. Question: "How much do you need to add to or subtract from your net investment income for a CFC or QEF with no section 1.1411-10(g) election in effect?" Help text: if you do NOT have a Regulations section 1.1411-10(g) election in effect for a CFC or QEF, you generally include in net investment income certain distributions of previously taxed income from the CFC or QEF that are not subject to regular income tax, and the investment interest expense you take into account for NIIT purposes may be increased or decreased from the amount taken into account for regular income tax — see Regulations section 1.1411-10 for the full rules (unvendored in this build; named rather than cited, invariant #3). Enter a positive number for a net increase, a negative number for a net decrease. Asked when: the filer owns stock, directly or indirectly, in a CFC or QEF and /writableNiitCfcAndQefRegulationElection is answered false or left unanswered. Unanswered posture: DEFAULTED to $0 through /niitLine6CfcQefNoElectionAdjustment — disclosed. Validation: Dollar, no Min/Max (signed — the source states both an increase and a decrease arm). What the answer feeds: Form 8960 line 6 → line 8 → line 12. LEAVE THIS BLANK OR ZERO whenever the per-holding /niitCfcQefHoldings collection is answered. The two boxes describe the same adjustment, so an amount in both is a contradiction and makes line 6 Incomplete rather than counting the adjustment twice.

Fact.Name: Form 8960 line 7, other modifications to investment income (writable)
Fact.Description:
Form 8960 Part I line 7, "Other modifications to investment income": the residual line the instructions use for items such as a net operating loss deduction properly allocable to net investment income and the other modifications described in the section 1411 regulations that lines 1 through 6 do not carry. It is a filer supplied residual by construction, so it is an intake in any build. Do NOT include Form 8814 line 12, a Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) box 14 code H amount, or the casualty and theft loss reported on Schedule A (Form 1040) line 15 here — all three are added for you (/form8814TotalLine12OtherIncome, /niitEstateTrustK1Box14CodeHTotal and /niitLine7CasualtyAndTheftLossScheduleALine15, the last already carrying the printed negative sign); entering any of them again here counts it twice. The same goes for working-capital interest and dividends reported inside Schedule C or Schedule F income: that amount has its own box (/writableNiitWorkingCapitalInterestAndDividendsInBusinessIncome) and is added for you.
WORKING CAPITAL IS NOT BACKED OUT HERE, and this is the one fence on this box that the printed instructions do not state for themselves. The instructions invite a NEGATIVE line 7 entry for business interest — "Interest income earned in the ordinary course of your non-section 1411 trade or business is excluded from NII. If this type of interest income is included on line 1, use line 7 to adjust your NII" — and a filer following that sentence literally would back out ALL of a business's interest and dividends. Section 1411(c)(3) forbids part of it: it applies a rule similar to section 469(e)(1)(B), under which "any income, gain, or loss which is attributable to an investment of working capital shall be treated as not derived in the ordinary course of a trade or business." So interest and dividends earned on the business's WORKING CAPITAL — its cash reserves, its short-term deposits, the return on money the business holds rather than deploys — stay in net investment income however the business itself is characterized under section 469, and a negative modification entered here must EXCLUDE them. The Form 8960 instructions never use the phrase "working capital" anywhere; the rule is statutory only, which is why it is stated here rather than quoted. Do not enter a section 1411 NOL deduction here either when the /niitNolYears loss-component collection is answered: that collection computes the applicable portion and carries it to line 7 as a negative amount, and a manual entry of the same deduction doubles it.

Fact.Name: Working-capital interest and dividends reported inside Schedule C or Schedule F income (writable)
Fact.Description:
SCREEN. Question: "How much interest or dividends did your business earn on money it was holding — its cash reserves, deposits or short-term investments — that you reported as business income rather than on Schedule B?" Help text: a business's return on the money it holds rather than deploys is INVESTMENT income for the net investment income tax even when the business itself is not an investment activity — section 1411(c)(3) applies a rule similar to section 469(e)(1)(B), under which income attributable to an investment of working capital is treated as NOT derived in the ordinary course of a trade or business. Schedule C line 6, "Interest (such as on notes and accounts receivable)", is where such an amount is reported; Schedule F's other-income line does the same job. Enter ONLY amounts that are inside your Schedule C or Schedule F figures.
